domaine-de-villaine.name: A. et P. de Villaine
domaine-de-villaine.line: The Bouzeron estate founded by Aubert de Villaine of the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and his wife Pamela, making pure, unshowy Côte Chalonnaise wines.
domaine-de-villaine.tell: This is the family estate of Aubert de Villaine, long the co-director of Romanée-Conti, down in the quieter Côte Chalonnaise. The reds are fresh, red fruited Pinot Noir with real finesse for the price. A smart pick for a guest who loves Burgundy but not grand cru prices.

albert-bichot.name: Albert Bichot
albert-bichot.line: A large family négociant in Beaune that also owns domaines, among them Clos Frantin in Nuits and Domaine du Pavillon in Pommard.
albert-bichot.tell: Bichot is a big Beaune house that owns its own vineyards as well as buying grapes; bottles marked Clos Frantin or Domaine du Pavillon come from those estates. The style is polished and dependable. A good way to give a guest a named village or premier cru from a trusted house.

albert-ponnelle.name: Albert Ponnelle
albert-ponnelle.line: A Beaune négociant house bottling village and premier cru wines across the Côte d'Or in a classic, traditional style.
albert-ponnelle.tell: Ponnelle is a long established Beaune house. Its Volnay is the gentle, perfumed side of the Côte de Beaune: red cherry, soft tannin, made to go with food. Ask the sommelier how this vintage is drinking.

antoine-jobard.name: Antoine Jobard
antoine-jobard.line: A Meursault family domaine famous for long lived, tightly wound white wines, which also makes small amounts of red from the Côte de Beaune.
antoine-jobard.tell: Jobard is a name white Burgundy lovers know well, so a red from this cellar is something of a curiosity. Expect a precise, firm Pinot Noir that rewards a little air. A good talking point for a guest who already drinks the whites.

antonin-guyon.name: Antonin Guyon
antonin-guyon.line: A family domaine based in Savigny-lès-Beaune with vineyards from the Hautes-Côtes to Corton and Volnay, making traditional, well structured reds.
antonin-guyon.tell: Guyon farms a wide spread of vineyards across both Côtes. Their Volnay Clos des Chênes comes from one of the village's best known premier crus, a slope that gives a bit more grip than most Volnay. Recommend it with roast meats and game birds.

antonin-rodet.name: Antonin Rodet
antonin-rodet.line: A Mercurey based négociant house bottling wines from across Burgundy, here a Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru.
antonin-rodet.tell: Rodet is a long standing house from the Côte Chalonnaise. Clos de Thorey is a premier cru in Nuits-Saint-Georges, so expect darker fruit and firmer tannin than the villages to the north. A sturdy partner for beef or duck.

arnaud-mortet.name: Arnaud Mortet
arnaud-mortet.line: The son of the late Denis Mortet, who now runs the family domaine and also bottles wines under his own name in Gevrey-Chambertin.
arnaud-mortet.tell: Arnaud took over the Mortet domaine and added a small range under his own label. The wines are deep coloured, ripe and carefully made Gevrey. A good choice for a guest who wants a powerful red Burgundy.

aurelien-verdet.name: Aurélien Verdet
aurelien-verdet.line: A small family domaine from the Hautes-Côtes de Nuits, organic for decades, making fresh, honest village wines including Morey-Saint-Denis.
aurelien-verdet.tell: Verdet is a small grower from the hills above the Côte de Nuits, working organically. His Morey-Saint-Denis is a straightforward, fresh village red at a fair price. A good pour for a table that wants real Burgundy without a big spend.

dugat-py.name: Domaine Bernard Dugat-Py
dugat-py.line: A cult Gevrey-Chambertin domaine, now run by Loïc Dugat-Py, known for very old vines, tiny yields and dense, concentrated, long lived reds.
dugat-py.tell: Dugat-Py is one of the most sought after names in Gevrey. Old vines and very low yields give deep, dark, powerful wines that need time and air. These are rare bottles: suggest decanting, and let the guest know they are holding something collectors chase.

bitouzet-prieur.name: Bitouzet-Prieur
bitouzet-prieur.line: A family domaine straddling Volnay and Meursault, making traditional, quietly classic Volnay and white Meursault.
bitouzet-prieur.tell: A traditional family estate. Their Volnay is the elegant, perfumed style the village is known for: red fruit, silky tannin, nothing forced. With some age now, it is a lovely partner for poultry and veal.

bouchard-pere-et-fils.name: Bouchard Père & Fils
bouchard-pere-et-fils.line: One of the largest landholders on the Côte d'Or, a historic Beaune house whose own premier and grand cru vineyards anchor a broad range.
bouchard-pere-et-fils.tell: Bouchard owns a large spread of top vineyards, especially in Beaune. Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus is their famous parcel in the Beaune Grèves premier cru. The half bottles here are a handy way to give a couple a proper premier cru Burgundy.

bruno-clavelier.name: Bruno Clavelier
bruno-clavelier.line: A Vosne-Romanée grower farming biodynamically, known for old vines and a terroir focused, transparent style across Vosne, Chambolle and Gevrey.
bruno-clavelier.tell: Clavelier farms old vines biodynamically and makes wines that show where they grow rather than how they were made. Expect fragrant, fine Pinot Noir with a savoury edge. A strong recommendation for a guest who likes Burgundy with detail and finesse.

bruno-colin.name: Bruno Colin
bruno-colin.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet grower, part of the large Colin family, best known for whites but also making reds from the southern Côte de Beaune.
bruno-colin.tell: Bruno Colin comes from one of Chassagne's best known families. His Santenay red is a bright, fresh Pinot Noir from old vines, a good value step into the Côte de Beaune. Easy with lighter meats and mushrooms.

camille-giroud.name: Camille Giroud
camille-giroud.line: A small Beaune négociant known for a traditional, unhurried style, with wines that are built to age rather than to impress young.
camille-giroud.tell: Giroud is a small Beaune house with a reputation for classic, age worthy reds. The Chambertin here has had time in bottle, and the Marsannay is a lighter, fresher village wine. Ask the sommelier how the older bottle is showing before you promise anything.

charles-audoin.name: Charles Audoin
charles-audoin.line: A family domaine in Marsannay, the northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits, making crisp, red fruited Pinot Noir from named sites.
charles-audoin.tell: Marsannay sits at the top of the Côte de Nuits and gives lighter, brighter reds. Audoin is a local family grower, and Les Favières is one of their named vineyards. A good value Burgundy for a guest who likes freshness.

claude-dugat.name: Domaine Claude Dugat
claude-dugat.line: A small, highly prized Gevrey-Chambertin domaine, cousin to Dugat-Py, making deep, rich wines in tiny quantities.
claude-dugat.tell: Claude Dugat's wines are scarce and much sought after. They are dark, generous and polished Gevrey with real depth. These are collector bottles: decant and serve with red meat or game.

coche-dury.name: Domaine Coche-Dury
coche-dury.line: The Meursault domaine whose white wines are among the most coveted in the world; its small production of reds is just as hard to find.
coche-dury.tell: Coche-Dury is a legendary Meursault name, famous for white wine. The reds, from Volnay, Monthélie, Auxey-Duresses and Pommard, are made in tiny amounts and rarely seen. For a guest who knows the name, this is the treat; the price reflects the scarcity, not the appellation.

comtesse-de-cherisey.name: Comtesse Bernard de Chérisey
comtesse-de-cherisey.line: A family estate in the hamlet of Blagny above Meursault and Puligny, owner of the La Genelotte premier cru.
comtesse-de-cherisey.tell: Blagny is a tiny hamlet high on the slope where reds carry the Blagny name. This is a rarely seen premier cru red with a fresh, mineral feel. A good choice for a curious guest who wants something off the beaten track.

david-duband.name: David Duband
david-duband.line: A grower based in the Hautes-Côtes de Nuits making fragrant, whole cluster influenced reds across the Côte de Nuits.
david-duband.tell: Duband is known for perfumed, lifted Pinot Noir with plenty of energy. His Nuits-Saint-Georges is a village wine with good structure. A nice match for duck or mushrooms.

denis-mortet.name: Domaine Denis Mortet
denis-mortet.line: A leading Gevrey-Chambertin domaine founded by the late Denis Mortet and now run by his son Arnaud, known for deep coloured, intense reds.
denis-mortet.tell: Mortet is one of the benchmark names in Gevrey. The wines are dark, concentrated and long, from the village wine Mes Cinq Terroirs up to the premier crus. A safe recommendation for a guest who wants a full bodied red Burgundy.

didier-fornerol.name: Didier Fornerol
didier-fornerol.line: A small grower in the southern Côte de Nuits making Côte de Nuits-Villages and other modest appellations with care.
didier-fornerol.tell: A small family grower from the villages at the southern end of the Côte de Nuits. Côte de Nuits-Villages gives honest, red fruited Pinot Noir at a gentle price. Good for a table that wants an easy, food friendly Burgundy.

domaine-af-gros.name: Domaine A.F. Gros
domaine-af-gros.line: The Pommard based domaine of Anne-Françoise Gros, of the Gros family of Vosne-Romanée, making supple, ripe reds across the Côte d'Or.
domaine-af-gros.tell: A.F. Gros belongs to the wide Gros family of Vosne-Romanée. Their Chambolle-Musigny is the fragrant, silky side of the Côte de Nuits. A gentle, crowd pleasing red Burgundy.

alex-moreau.name: Domaine Alex Moreau
alex-moreau.line: The newer label of Alex Moreau, of the Bernard Moreau family in Chassagne-Montrachet, focused on precise wines from family vineyards.
alex-moreau.tell: Alex Moreau comes from a well regarded Chassagne family and now bottles under his own name. The red Chassagne from old vines is a fresh, firm Pinot Noir, and the Passe-Tout-Grains is a light, easy blend of Pinot and Gamay. Both suit lighter meat dishes.

anne-gros.name: Domaine Anne Gros
anne-gros.line: One of Vosne-Romanée's most admired domaines, run by Anne Gros, known for silky, pure, elegant reds from Bourgogne up to Richebourg.
anne-gros.tell: Anne Gros makes some of the most graceful wines in Vosne-Romanée. Even the regional wines show polish, and the grand crus are rare and refined. A strong recommendation for a guest who prizes elegance over power.

domaine-arlaud.name: Domaine Arlaud
domaine-arlaud.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine farming biodynamically, making bright, fresh, finely tuned reds from regional wine to grand cru.
domaine-arlaud.tell: Arlaud is a Morey family estate known for clean, energetic Pinot Noir. The Roncevie is their excellent Bourgogne, and the grand cru Clos Saint-Denis is a serious, fragrant wine. Good value at every level.

armand-rousseau.name: Domaine Armand Rousseau
armand-rousseau.line: Perhaps the most famous name in Gevrey-Chambertin, revered for elegant, perfumed reds from Chambertin and the Clos Saint-Jacques premier cru.
armand-rousseau.tell: Rousseau is a reference point for all of Burgundy. Clos Saint-Jacques is a premier cru often spoken of in the same breath as the grand crus. A trophy bottle: handle it with ceremony and suggest a gentle decant.

bernard-moreau.name: Domaine Bernard Moreau et Fils
bernard-moreau.line: A well regarded Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine, better known for white wine, also making fresh, firm red Chassagne.
bernard-moreau.tell: Moreau is a respected Chassagne family. Red Chassagne is less known than the whites but can be very good value, and this old vine bottling has depth. A good match for pork or roast chicken.

berthelemot.name: Domaine Berthelemot
berthelemot.line: A Côte de Beaune domaine making wines across several villages, here a Monthélie red with some bottle age.
berthelemot.tell: Monthélie sits next to Volnay and gives similar charm for less money. This bottle has a few years on it, so expect softer fruit and savoury notes. An easy value pick for a guest who likes mature red.

billard-gonnet.name: Domaine Billard-Gonnet
billard-gonnet.line: A traditional Pommard family domaine with holdings in the village's top premier crus, including Les Rugiens.
billard-gonnet.tell: Billard-Gonnet is a Pommard family estate. Les Rugiens is Pommard's most famous premier cru, giving a firm, deep red that softens with age. A good pick with beef or lamb.

blain-gagnard.name: Domaine Blain-Gagnard
blain-gagnard.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine with fine white holdings that also makes red Chassagne in a supple, fresh style.
blain-gagnard.tell: Blain-Gagnard is a respected Chassagne name. Their red Chassagne is a bright, medium bodied Pinot Noir, an under the radar value on a list this deep. Good with chicken, pork or fish in a red wine sauce.

bruno-clair.name: Domaine Bruno Clair
bruno-clair.line: A leading Marsannay domaine with vineyards from Marsannay to Gevrey and Savigny, making clean, precise, classically built reds.
bruno-clair.tell: Bruno Clair is one of the top growers in the northern Côte de Nuits. La Dominode is an old vine premier cru in Savigny-lès-Beaune, and gives a structured, fragrant wine for a fair price. A good value premier cru recommendation.

camille-thiriet.name: Domaine Camille Thiriet
camille-thiriet.line: A young domaine in the southern Côte de Nuits making lively reds from Côte de Nuits-Villages vineyards.
camille-thiriet.tell: Camille Thiriet is a newer name making fresh, vibrant Pinot Noir from small named sites in the Côte de Nuits-Villages. These are bright and juicy rather than heavy. A fun pick for a guest who likes natural leaning wines.

domaine-collotte.name: Domaine Collotte
domaine-collotte.line: A family grower in Marsannay, making village wines from named sites; this bottle has considerable age.
domaine-collotte.tell: Marsannay gives light, red fruited Pinot Noir. This is an older bottle, so expect gentle, savoury flavours rather than fresh fruit. Ask the sommelier to check it before recommending it as a showpiece.

comte-georges-de-vogue.name: Domaine Comte Georges de Vogüé
comte-georges-de-vogue.line: The historic Chambolle-Musigny domaine and the largest owner of the Musigny grand cru, making powerful, slow developing wines.
comte-georges-de-vogue.tell: De Vogüé owns most of the Musigny grand cru and is one of Burgundy's great names. The wines are deep and structured when young and need years to open. Recommend decanting, and treat any bottle here as a special occasion wine.

domaine-d-eugenie.name: Domaine d'Eugénie
domaine-d-eugenie.line: The Vosne-Romanée domaine owned by the Pinault family, also owners of Château Latour, built on the former Engel vineyards.
domaine-d-eugenie.tell: Eugénie is owned by the same family as Château Latour, so a Bordeaux lover may like the connection. Aux Brûlées is a respected Vosne premier cru giving rich, spicy Pinot Noir. A good bridge for a guest moving from Bordeaux to Burgundy.

daniel-rion.name: Domaine Daniel Rion & Fils
daniel-rion.line: A family domaine in Prémeaux, at the southern end of Nuits-Saint-Georges, making firm, classic reds across the Côte de Nuits.
daniel-rion.tell: Rion is a family estate in the Nuits-Saint-Georges area. Their village Nuits from Les Lavières is a sturdy, dark fruited red. A good partner for steak or game.

dubreuil-fontaine.name: Domaine Dubreuil-Fontaine
dubreuil-fontaine.line: A family domaine in Pernand-Vergelesses with holdings on the hill of Corton, making traditional, firm reds that age well.
dubreuil-fontaine.tell: Dubreuil-Fontaine is rooted on the hill of Corton. Their Corton grand crus, Bressandes, Clos du Roi and Perrières, are firm, structured reds, and several here have some age. Good value grand cru for red meat.

domaine-dujac.name: Domaine Dujac
domaine-dujac.line: The Morey-Saint-Denis domaine founded by Jacques Seysses and run by his family, known for whole cluster fermentation and silky, perfumed reds.
domaine-dujac.tell: Dujac is one of Burgundy's most loved names. They ferment with whole bunches, which gives a spicy, floral lift and silky texture; Dujac Fils et Père is the family's négociant label from bought grapes. From village wine to Clos de la Roche, these are elegant, fragrant bottles.

faiveley.name: Domaine Faiveley
faiveley.line: A historic Nuits-Saint-Georges house and one of Burgundy's biggest vineyard owners, making structured, modern, well made reds from Mercurey to Chambertin.
faiveley.tell: Faiveley owns a remarkable spread of vineyards, many in the Côte de Nuits and the Côte Chalonnaise. The reds are dark, firm and reliable, from Mercurey up to the Chambertin grand crus. A safe, quality recommendation at almost any price.

fourrier.name: Domaine Fourrier
fourrier.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin domaine run by Jean-Marie Fourrier, prized for old vines and pure, transparent, fragrant reds.
fourrier.tell: Fourrier is one of the most sought after growers in Gevrey. The wines are fresh, fragrant and precise rather than heavy, with old vines throughout. Clos Saint-Jacques is the star; the village Vieilles Vignes is a lovely entry point.

francois-lumpp.name: Domaine François Lumpp
francois-lumpp.line: A Givry grower in the Côte Chalonnaise, known as one of the village's leading names for red Pinot Noir.
francois-lumpp.tell: Lumpp is a leading name in Givry, south of the Côte d'Or. His wines are bright, red fruited and well made, good value next to the big villages. A friendly, food ready red Burgundy.

geantet-pansiot.name: Domaine Geantet-Pansiot
geantet-pansiot.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin family domaine making generous, ripe and approachable reds from village and premier cru sites.
geantet-pansiot.tell: Geantet-Pansiot makes a rich, rounded style of Gevrey that is easy to enjoy young. The old vine bottlings are a good step up. A safe recommendation for a guest who wants fruit and body.

mugneret-gibourg.name: Domaine Georges Mugneret-Gibourg
mugneret-gibourg.line: A small, much admired Vosne-Romanée domaine run by the Mugneret sisters, celebrated for silky, perfumed, beautifully balanced reds.
mugneret-gibourg.tell: Mugneret-Gibourg is a quiet star of Vosne-Romanée. The wines have finesse, fragrance and a silky texture at every level, from Bourgogne to Échezeaux. These bottles are scarce; any of them is a lovely choice for a guest who knows Burgundy.

georges-roumier.name: Domaine Georges Roumier
georges-roumier.line: The Chambolle-Musigny domaine of Christophe Roumier, one of the most celebrated names in Burgundy, known for intense, precise reds.
georges-roumier.tell: Roumier is among the most sought after names in all of Burgundy. Bonnes-Mares and the Clos de la Bussière monopole in Morey are both here. These wines are rare and highly prized; suggest decanting and treat them as the occasion.

gros-frere-et-soeur.name: Domaine Gros Frère et Soeur
gros-frere-et-soeur.line: A Vosne-Romanée domaine of the Gros family, making ripe, plush reds including a Clos Vougeot from the Musigni parcel.
gros-frere-et-soeur.tell: Another branch of the Gros family in Vosne-Romanée, with a generous, ripe style. Their Clos Vougeot comes from the top of the vineyard near Musigny. A good bet for a guest who likes a fuller Burgundy.

genot-boulanger.name: Domaine Génot-Boulanger
genot-boulanger.line: A Côte de Beaune domaine with vineyards spread from Mercurey to Clos Vougeot, making clean, precise reds and whites.
genot-boulanger.tell: Génot-Boulanger farms across the Côte de Beaune and beyond. Their reds here range from Aloxe-Corton and Pommard to Corton and Clos Vougeot grand cru. A reliable choice with balanced, modern Pinot Noir.

gerard-raphet.name: Domaine Gérard Raphet
gerard-raphet.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine with a range across Gevrey, Morey, Chambolle and Clos Vougeot, in a traditional style.
gerard-raphet.tell: Raphet is a quiet family estate in Morey-Saint-Denis. The wines are traditional, firm and fruity, from village wines up to Clos Vougeot. A good value name on a list of famous ones.

henri-gouges.name: Domaine Henri Gouges
henri-gouges.line: The reference domaine of Nuits-Saint-Georges, making firm, dark, long lived reds from the village's best premier crus.
henri-gouges.tell: Gouges is the name most people think of in Nuits-Saint-Georges. The wines are sturdy and structured, with dark fruit and an earthy edge, and they age very well. The half bottles are a great option for two guests with red meat.

henri-prudhon.name: Domaine Henri Prudhon
henri-prudhon.line: A Saint-Aubin family domaine, best known for white wine, also making red Saint-Aubin premier cru.
henri-prudhon.tell: Saint-Aubin sits in a side valley behind Puligny and Chassagne. Its reds are light and fresh, and these bottles have some age. A modest price for a premier cru red.

hubert-lamy.name: Domaine Hubert Lamy
hubert-lamy.line: A Saint-Aubin domaine famous for precise white wines from densely planted vines, also making small amounts of red.
hubert-lamy.tell: Lamy is one of the stars of Saint-Aubin, mainly for whites. This red Santenay is a rarer bottling, fresh and finely made. A good conversation bottle for a guest who knows the name.

jacques-girardin.name: Domaine Jacques Girardin
jacques-girardin.line: A Santenay family domaine making reds from Santenay and neighbouring villages including Pommard.
jacques-girardin.tell: A family grower from Santenay at the southern end of the Côte de Beaune. The Santenay Clos Rousseau premier cru and the Pommard are honest, firm reds. Good value with roasts.

justin-girardin.name: Domaine Justin Girardin
justin-girardin.line: A Santenay family domaine making Côte de Beaune reds and whites, here a village Pommard.
justin-girardin.tell: A family grower from Santenay. Village Pommard gives a firm, dark fruited red. A sensible value choice for steak.

jean-grivot.name: Domaine Jean Grivot
jean-grivot.line: A leading Vosne-Romanée domaine run by Étienne Grivot and family, making fine, expressive reds from village wine to Richebourg.
jean-grivot.tell: Grivot is one of the great Vosne-Romanée names, with a range from village Vosne up to Richebourg. The wines are refined and long, with a lovely spicy fruit. A safe, distinguished choice at many price points.

jean-marie-bouzereau.name: Domaine Jean-Marie Bouzereau
jean-marie-bouzereau.line: A Meursault family domaine, part of the large Bouzereau clan, also making red from the Santenots vineyard.
jean-marie-bouzereau.tell: Santenots lies in Meursault but its red wine is sold as Volnay premier cru. Expect a firmer, slightly darker Volnay. A good match for duck or pork.

jean-marc-pavelot.name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pavelot
jean-marc-pavelot.line: A family domaine in Savigny-lès-Beaune making fresh, well priced reds, including Beaune premier cru.
jean-marc-pavelot.tell: Pavelot is a respected Savigny family. Their Beaune Bressandes premier cru is a balanced, red fruited wine at a fair price. A friendly pick for most red meats.

jean-michel-gaunoux.name: Domaine Jean-Michel Gaunoux
jean-michel-gaunoux.line: A Meursault domaine of the Gaunoux family, making traditional Côte de Beaune wines, including red Pommard.
jean-michel-gaunoux.tell: Gaunoux makes traditional Burgundy that rewards patience. This Pommard premier cru has had time to soften. A good value mature red for game or beef.

joseph-drouhin.name: Joseph Drouhin
joseph-drouhin.line: A family owned Beaune house with large organic and biodynamic holdings, known for graceful, elegant wines and its Beaune Clos des Mouches.
joseph-drouhin.tell: Drouhin is one of Beaune's great family houses, with a style built on elegance. Clos des Mouches is their signature Beaune premier cru, and they also own parcels in Musigny and Les Amoureuses. A trusted name for any guest.

joseph-voillot.name: Domaine Joseph Voillot
joseph-voillot.line: A Volnay family domaine making traditional, fragrant reds from Volnay and Pommard.
joseph-voillot.tell: Voillot is a classic Volnay grower. The old vine Volnay and Bourgogne are charming, red fruited and soft. Easy recommendations with poultry and pork.

domaine-larue.name: Domaine Larue
domaine-larue.line: A family domaine based in Saint-Aubin making wines from Saint-Aubin, Chassagne-Montrachet and Blagny.
domaine-larue.tell: Larue is a family grower from Saint-Aubin. Their red Chassagne La Boudriotte and Blagny premier cru are firm and fresh. Good value premier cru reds.

louis-jadot.name: Louis Jadot
louis-jadot.line: One of the great Beaune houses, owning large holdings across the Côte d'Or and Beaujolais and bottling an enormous range of reds.
louis-jadot.tell: Jadot is one of Burgundy's most recognised names, owning vineyards from Beaujolais up to Chambertin. The quality is very consistent, and bottles marked Domaine come from their own vineyards. The half bottle is a handy option for a couple.

lucien-boillot.name: Domaine Lucien Boillot et Fils
lucien-boillot.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin based family domaine, run by Pierre Boillot, with vineyards in Gevrey, Nuits, Pommard and Volnay.
lucien-boillot.tell: Boillot is a family estate with roots in both the Côte de Nuits and the Côte de Beaune. The wines are deep and well structured. Their Pommard and Volnay premier crus are good value for the quality.

domaine-matrot.name: Domaine Matrot
domaine-matrot.line: A Meursault family domaine, run by Thierry and Pascale Matrot, known mostly for whites, also making reds from the southern Côte de Beaune.
domaine-matrot.tell: Matrot is a well known Meursault family. Their reds from Saint-Aubin and Maranges are light, fresh and modestly priced. Good choices for a lighter meal.

michel-magnien.name: Domaine Michel Magnien
michel-magnien.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine, run by Frédéric Magnien, farming organically and making fresh, transparent reds.
michel-magnien.tell: The Magnien family domaine in Morey-Saint-Denis. The wines are fresh and focused, with a light touch. The Chambolle premier cru Les Sentiers is fragrant and fine.

frederic-magnien.name: Frédéric Magnien
frederic-magnien.line: The négociant label of Frédéric Magnien in Morey-Saint-Denis, bottling wines from bought grapes across the Côte de Nuits.
frederic-magnien.tell: Frédéric Magnien buys grapes from growers across the Côte de Nuits and makes them in Morey. The wines are fresh and clear. A good value route into Clos Vougeot and Morey.

mongeard-mugneret.name: Domaine Mongeard-Mugneret
mongeard-mugneret.line: A Vosne-Romanée family domaine with a broad range, including Échezeaux and Richebourg, in a ripe, generous style.
mongeard-mugneret.tell: Mongeard-Mugneret is a large Vosne family estate. The wines are generous and approachable, from Hautes-Côtes up to Richebourg. A good way to give a guest a grand cru at a gentler price.

monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.name: Domaine Monthelie-Douhairet-Porcheret
monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.line: A historic Monthélie domaine making traditional, long lived reds from Monthélie, Volnay and Pommard.
monthelie-douhairet-porcheret.tell: This Monthélie estate makes traditional wines that need time. The Volnay Champans and Pommard premier crus are firm and serious. Good value for a guest who likes classic Burgundy.

meo-camuzet.name: Domaine Méo-Camuzet
meo-camuzet.line: A leading Vosne-Romanée domaine run by Jean-Nicolas Méo, linked to the legendary Henri Jayer, making rich, polished reds.
meo-camuzet.tell: Méo-Camuzet is one of Vosne's top names; Henri Jayer once farmed some of its vines. The wines are ripe, deep and polished. Bottles marked Frère et Soeurs are the négociant range from bought grapes, a gentler price for the same hand.

domaine-newman.name: Domaine Newman
domaine-newman.line: A small domaine with grand cru holdings in the Côte de Nuits, here a Bonnes-Mares.
domaine-newman.tell: Domaine Newman is a small estate with parcels in some famous grand crus. Bonnes-Mares gives a deep, structured wine. Comparatively modest in price for a grand cru; ask the sommelier how this bottle is drinking.

paul-garaudet.name: Domaine Paul Garaudet
paul-garaudet.line: A Monthélie family domaine making honest, fruity reds from Monthélie and neighbouring Volnay.
paul-garaudet.tell: A small family grower in Monthélie, a village that offers Volnay like charm for less. Cuvée Paul is fresh and red fruited. A friendly, value red.

paul-pillot.name: Domaine Paul Pillot
paul-pillot.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine known for very fine whites and fresh, bright reds from Chassagne and Santenay.
paul-pillot.tell: Pillot is a top Chassagne family. Red Chassagne and Santenay are under the radar values, light and fresh. Clos Saint-Jean is a premier cru that gives a bit more depth.

pierre-andre.name: Domaine Pierre André
pierre-andre.line: A Côte de Beaune house bottling wines from across the Côte, here Pommard Clos de la Commaraine.
pierre-andre.tell: Clos de la Commaraine is a walled premier cru in Pommard. Expect a firm, dark fruited red with a few years of age. A good match for beef.

pierre-gelin.name: Domaine Pierre Gelin
pierre-gelin.line: A Fixin family domaine and owner of the Clos Napoléon premier cru, making firm, rustic reds and a Chambertin Clos de Bèze.
pierre-gelin.tell: Gelin is Fixin's best known name, a village next to Gevrey that gives sturdy reds at good prices. Clos Napoléon is their own walled vineyard. The Clos de Bèze is the grand cru treat.

pierre-morey.name: Domaine Pierre Morey
pierre-morey.line: A Meursault domaine farmed biodynamically, best known for whites, also making red Pommard.
pierre-morey.tell: Pierre Morey is a famous name in Meursault whites. This Pommard Grands Épenots has some age, giving a softened, savoury red. A good pick for game birds or beef.

domaine-ponsot.name: Domaine Ponsot
domaine-ponsot.line: A famous Morey-Saint-Denis domaine, a great name in Clos de la Roche, known for a traditional style without new oak and cuvées named after birds and insects.
domaine-ponsot.tell: Ponsot is one of the great Morey names, with grand crus from Clos de la Roche to Chambertin. Cuvée names like Grives, Pinson and Abeille mean thrush, finch and bee. The wines are fragrant and long; suggest decanting the grand crus.

laurent-ponsot.name: Laurent Ponsot
laurent-ponsot.line: The house Laurent Ponsot founded after leaving his family domaine, with cuvées named after trees.
laurent-ponsot.tell: Laurent Ponsot ran his family's Morey domaine for decades before starting his own house. Cuvée de l'Aulne, named for the alder tree, is a village Gevrey. A good talking point for a guest who knows the Ponsot name.

ramonet.name: Domaine Ramonet
ramonet.line: A legendary Chassagne-Montrachet domaine, famous for white wine, also making serious red Chassagne.
ramonet.tell: Ramonet is one of the most revered names in white Burgundy. Their red Chassagne is firm, fresh and long lived, and Clos Saint-Jean is a classic premier cru. A clever choice for a red drinker who wants a great name.

regnaudot.name: Domaine Regnaudot
regnaudot.line: A family grower in Maranges, the southernmost village of the Côte de Beaune, making sturdy, good value reds.
regnaudot.tell: Maranges is the last village at the south of the Côte de Beaune, and it gives firm, fruity reds at fair prices. Regnaudot is a local family. These are some of the best value premier crus on the list.

robert-chevillon.name: Domaine Robert Chevillon
robert-chevillon.line: A benchmark Nuits-Saint-Georges domaine with old vines across the village's top premier crus, making classic, structured reds.
robert-chevillon.tell: Chevillon is one of the great names of Nuits. The premier crus, from Les Saints-Georges to Les Vaucrains, show the village's deep fruit and firm tannin. Excellent with beef or game.

roblet-monnot.name: Domaine Roblet-Monnot
roblet-monnot.line: A small Volnay domaine making fragrant, finely textured reds from old vines.
roblet-monnot.tell: Roblet-Monnot is a small Volnay grower. Their Saint-François is fragrant and silky, the charming side of the Côte de Beaune. A lovely pick with chicken or duck.

domaine-roulot.name: Domaine Roulot
domaine-roulot.line: A celebrated Meursault domaine run by Jean-Marc Roulot, famous for pure white wines, which also makes a little red Monthélie.
domaine-roulot.tell: Roulot is one of the most sought after names in Meursault whites. The red Monthélie is a rare, fresh, finely made Pinot Noir. A treat for a guest who knows the name.

domaine-saint-martin.name: Domaine Saint-Martin
domaine-saint-martin.line: A little seen Burgundy name, here a Bonnes-Mares grand cru with some bottle age.
domaine-saint-martin.tell: A rarely seen bottling of Bonnes-Mares, the grand cru shared by Chambolle and Morey. This bottle has had years to soften. Ask the sommelier about the producer and how it is drinking.

serafin.name: Domaine Serafin
serafin.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin family domaine known for deep, ripe reds with generous oak and old vines.
serafin.tell: Serafin makes rich, dark and polished Gevrey, with old vines and generous oak. The premier crus Cazetiers and Corbeaux are powerful. A good match for steak.

domaine-serrigny.name: Domaine Serrigny
domaine-serrigny.line: A small Côte de Beaune grower, here a village Savigny-lès-Beaune.
domaine-serrigny.tell: Savigny-lès-Beaune gives fresh, red fruited Pinot Noir at friendly prices. A good value choice for a lighter red with chicken or pork.

sylvie-esmonin.name: Domaine Sylvie Esmonin
sylvie-esmonin.line: A Gevrey-Chambertin domaine with a parcel of the famous Clos Saint-Jacques, making traditional, whole cluster influenced reds.
sylvie-esmonin.tell: Sylvie Esmonin makes classic, savoury Gevrey with plenty of character. Her Clos Saint-Jacques is from one of Gevrey's most famous premier crus. A good pick for a guest who likes traditional Burgundy.

taupenot-merme.name: Domaine Taupenot-Merme
taupenot-merme.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine with grand cru holdings, here Mazoyères-Chambertin.
taupenot-merme.tell: Taupenot-Merme is a family estate in Morey. Mazoyères-Chambertin is a grand cru next to Charmes, giving a rich, ripe red. Good value for a grand cru.

marchand-tawse.name: Marchand-Tawse and Domaine Tawse
marchand-tawse.line: The Nuits-Saint-Georges house of winemaker Pascal Marchand and Canadian owner Moray Tawse: a négociant range plus the Domaine Tawse estate wines.
marchand-tawse.tell: Pascal Marchand is a well known winemaker in Burgundy. Marchand-Tawse bottles from bought grapes, while Domaine Tawse wines come from their own vines. Their Savigny Lavières and Volnay Frémiets are fragrant, well priced premier crus.

tollot-beaut.name: Domaine Tollot-Beaut
tollot-beaut.line: A Chorey-lès-Beaune family domaine making ripe, generous reds from Chorey, Savigny, Beaune, Aloxe-Corton and Corton.
tollot-beaut.tell: Tollot-Beaut is a reliable family estate known for ripe, fruity, crowd pleasing reds. Chorey-lès-Beaune is one of the best values on the list, and the Corton Bressandes is a step up. Safe recommendations.

domaine-trapet.name: Domaine Trapet
domaine-trapet.line: A historic Gevrey-Chambertin domaine run biodynamically by Jean-Louis Trapet, with Chambertin, Latricières and Chapelle-Chambertin.
domaine-trapet.tell: Trapet is a long established Gevrey family with excellent grand crus. The wines are pure and fragrant. Capita is listed among the Gevrey premier crus; ask the sommelier about it.

vincent-girardin.name: Domaine Vincent Girardin
vincent-girardin.line: A Meursault based house making wines across the Côte de Beaune, here a village Beaune.
vincent-girardin.tell: Village Beaune gives a round, red fruited Pinot Noir. Girardin is a known Côte de Beaune name. A good value, easy red.

domaine-de-courcel.name: Domaine de Courcel
domaine-de-courcel.line: A historic Pommard family domaine, owner of a large share of the Grand Clos des Épenots, making whole cluster, long lived reds.
domaine-de-courcel.tell: Courcel is one of Pommard's best domaines. Its Grand Clos des Épenots is the flagship, a firm, fragrant wine that ages for years. A strong pick for a guest who wants a serious Côte de Beaune red.

de-montille.name: Domaine de Montille
de-montille.line: A Volnay family domaine, run by Étienne de Montille, known for elegant, whole cluster reds; Maison de Montille is its négociant label.
de-montille.tell: De Montille is a leading Volnay family making fragrant, fresh, finely structured wines. Pommard Rugiens and Beaune Sizies are classic premier crus. A trusted choice.

pousse-d-or.name: Domaine de la Pousse d'Or
pousse-d-or.line: A historic Volnay domaine with several walled monopole vineyards, including Clos de la Bousse d'Or and Clos des 60 Ouvrées.
pousse-d-or.tell: Pousse d'Or owns walled vineyards in Volnay and Pommard. The style is ripe and polished, and Clos de la Bousse d'Or is their signature. A safe premier cru Volnay recommendation.

domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.line: The most famous estate in Burgundy, sole owner of Romanée-Conti and La Tâche, with holdings in Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, Échezeaux and Grands-Échezeaux.
domaine-de-la-romanee-conti.tell: DRC is the most celebrated wine estate in the world for many collectors. Romanée-Conti and La Tâche are wholly owned grand crus. These bottles are extremely rare; involve the sommelier for service, decanting and any questions about the vintage.

domaine-de-la-vougeraie.name: Domaine de la Vougeraie
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.line: The Boisset family's Côte d'Or estate, farmed biodynamically, making polished reds from many villages.
domaine-de-la-vougeraie.tell: Vougeraie is the Boisset family's estate, farmed biodynamically. Aux Thorey is a Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru with depth and spice. A good modern Burgundy pick.

comtes-lafon.name: Domaine des Comtes Lafon
comtes-lafon.line: A great Meursault name, famous for whites, whose red Volnay Santenots-du-Milieu is a long lived, serious wine.
comtes-lafon.tell: Lafon is one of the greatest names in white Burgundy. Their red Volnay Santenots-du-Milieu is firm and deep for Volnay. A fine choice for a guest who knows the name.

clos-des-lambrays.name: Domaine des Lambrays
clos-des-lambrays.line: Owner of nearly all of the Clos des Lambrays grand cru in Morey-Saint-Denis, now owned by the LVMH group.
clos-des-lambrays.tell: Clos des Lambrays is a grand cru that this domaine owns almost entirely. The wine is fragrant, fine and often made with whole bunches. A special occasion Burgundy.

domaine-dubois.name: Domaine Dubois
domaine-dubois.line: A Côte de Beaune family grower, here a Chorey-lès-Beaune with real bottle age.
domaine-dubois.tell: Chorey-lès-Beaune is a modest village giving soft, fruity reds. This bottle is mature, so expect savoury, gentle flavours. One of the cheapest reds in the section.

dureuil-janthial.name: Domaine Dureuil-Janthial
dureuil-janthial.line: A leading Rully domaine in the Côte Chalonnaise, making fresh, precise reds and whites.
dureuil-janthial.tell: Dureuil-Janthial is one of the best names in Rully. Their red is bright and crisp, an excellent value Burgundy. Good with lighter meats.

francois-bertheau.name: Domaine François Bertheau
francois-bertheau.line: A small Chambolle-Musigny family domaine, here a bottle of the famous Les Amoureuses premier cru.
francois-bertheau.tell: Les Amoureuses is Chambolle's most famous premier cru, often priced like a grand cru. Bertheau is a small local family. A fragrant, silky red for a special evening.

francois-mikulski.name: François Mikulski
francois-mikulski.line: A Meursault grower known mainly for whites, also making red Pommard.
francois-mikulski.tell: Mikulski is a respected Meursault name. This village Pommard is a firm, dark fruited red. A good match for steak.

hubert-lignier.name: Domaine Hubert Lignier
hubert-lignier.line: A Morey-Saint-Denis family domaine making deep, traditional reds from village wine up to Clos de la Roche.
hubert-lignier.tell: Lignier is a respected Morey family. The wines are deep and classic, with a long life. Clos de la Roche is their grand cru; the Morey premier crus are good value.

hudelot-baillet.name: Domaine Hudelot-Baillet
hudelot-baillet.line: A Chambolle-Musigny family domaine making fresh, fragrant reds.
hudelot-baillet.tell: Hudelot-Baillet is a Chambolle family grower. Their reds are fragrant and fresh. The old vine Chambolle is a lovely silky red with chicken or duck.

jacques-frederic-mugnier.name: Domaine Jacques-Frédéric Mugnier
jacques-frederic-mugnier.line: A celebrated Chambolle-Musigny domaine, run by Frédéric Mugnier, known for weightless, ethereal reds from Musigny and Bonnes-Mares.
jacques-frederic-mugnier.tell: Mugnier is one of the most admired names in Chambolle. The wines are delicate, fragrant and long. Bonnes-Mares here is a rare treat; recommend it to a guest who loves finesse.

jean-chauvenet.name: Domaine Jean Chauvenet
jean-chauvenet.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges family domaine making classic, firm village and premier cru wines.
jean-chauvenet.tell: Chauvenet is a traditional Nuits family. The village Nuits is a sturdy, dark red. A good value match for steak.

jerome-galeyrand.name: Jérôme Galeyrand
jerome-galeyrand.line: A small grower and négociant based near Gevrey-Chambertin making fresh, lively reds.
jerome-galeyrand.tell: Galeyrand is a small producer making bright, fresh Pinot Noir. En Billard is a village Gevrey site. A good value pick for a lighter red.

julien-cruchandeau.name: Julien Cruchandeau
julien-cruchandeau.line: A small grower making wines from the Hautes-Côtes and lesser known villages, here Ladoix.
julien-cruchandeau.tell: Ladoix sits beside Corton and gives sturdy, good value reds. Les Ranches is a named site there. A gentle priced, older red.

kalin-cellars.name: Kalin Cellars
kalin-cellars.line: A small California winery that also bottles wine from Burgundy vineyards, here Beaune reds from 2001.
kalin-cellars.tell: Kalin Cellars is a California winery known for holding wines before release. These Beaune reds from 2001 are rare. Ask the sommelier about the story and how they are drinking before you recommend them.

lequin-colin.name: Domaine Lequin-Colin
lequin-colin.line: A Santenay family domaine making wines across the southern Côte de Beaune.
lequin-colin.tell: Lequin-Colin is a family grower from Santenay. Their village Pommard Les Noizons is a firm, fruity red. A sound choice with beef.

maison-leroy.name: Maison Leroy
maison-leroy.line: The négociant house of Lalou Bize-Leroy, one of Burgundy's most legendary figures, known for holding wines until ready.
maison-leroy.tell: Leroy is one of the most legendary names in Burgundy. Their négociant wines are bought and held until they are ready. A rare, prized Beaune premier cru for a guest who knows.

maison-champy.name: Maison Champy
maison-champy.line: A historic Beaune négociant house making wines from across the Côte d'Or.
maison-champy.tell: Champy is an old Beaune house. These bottles range from a young Volnay to grand crus with some age. A dependable name.

marquis-d-angerville.name: Marquis d'Angerville
marquis-d-angerville.line: The great Volnay domaine, owner of the Clos des Ducs monopole, making pure, fragrant reds, farmed biodynamically.
marquis-d-angerville.tell: D'Angerville is perhaps the most famous name in Volnay. Clos des Ducs is their walled vineyard; Champans, Taillepieds and Caillerets are top premier crus. Elegant, fragrant and long lived.

michel-lafarge.name: Domaine Michel Lafarge
michel-lafarge.line: A leading Volnay family domaine, farmed biodynamically, making traditional, long lived reds including the Clos du Château des Ducs monopole.
michel-lafarge.tell: Lafarge is one of the great Volnay families. Clos des Chênes and their own Clos du Château des Ducs are classic premier crus. Pure, fragrant and long lived.

moillard-grivot.name: Moillard-Grivot
moillard-grivot.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges négociant house, here a Mercurey red with some age.
moillard-grivot.tell: Mercurey in the Côte Chalonnaise gives sturdy, red fruited reds. This one is from 2013, so it has softened. One of the gentlest prices among the reds.

nicolas-potel.name: Nicolas Potel
nicolas-potel.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges négociant house bearing the name of its founder, winemaker Nicolas Potel.
nicolas-potel.tell: The house bottles wines from bought grapes across the Côte d'Or. The Romanée-Saint-Vivant here is a grand cru at a gentler price than most. Ask the sommelier how these older bottles are showing.

olivier-bernstein.name: Olivier Bernstein
olivier-bernstein.line: A small, high end négociant specialising in grand and premier cru Côte de Nuits wines, with a polished, concentrated style.
olivier-bernstein.tell: Bernstein makes a small range of top Côte de Nuits wines from bought grapes. The style is polished, deep and generous. Gevrey Cazetiers and Champeaux are fine premier crus.

remoissenet.name: Remoissenet Père et Fils
remoissenet.line: A Beaune négociant famous for a deep cellar of old vintages, here Richebourg, Clos Vougeot and Volnay going back to the 1950s.
remoissenet.tell: Remoissenet is known for its deep stocks of old Burgundy. These bottles go back decades; their state can vary from bottle to bottle. Involve the sommelier before recommending any of them.

thibault-liger-belair.name: Domaine Thibault Liger-Belair
thibault-liger-belair.line: A Nuits-Saint-Georges domaine farmed biodynamically, making fresh, precise reds; Les Saints-Georges is its flagship premier cru.
thibault-liger-belair.tell: Thibault Liger-Belair makes vibrant, fragrant wines. Les Saints-Georges is Nuits' most famous premier cru. A strong recommendation with beef or game.

vincent-et-sophie-morey.name: Vincent & Sophie Morey
vincent-et-sophie-morey.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet family domaine making wines from Chassagne, Santenay and Maranges.
vincent-et-sophie-morey.tell: The Morey family of Chassagne makes clean, fresh wines. Maranges La Fussière is a fresh, fruity premier cru. Good value.

chateau-de-la-maltroye.name: Château de la Maltroye
chateau-de-la-maltroye.line: A Chassagne-Montrachet estate making reds and whites from Chassagne and neighbouring villages.
chateau-de-la-maltroye.tell: Maltroye is a Chassagne estate with a château. Red Chassagne is a bright, fresh Pinot Noir. A smart value pick.

domaine-labet-beaune.name: Domaine Labet (Beaune)
domaine-labet-beaune.line: A Beaune premier cru bottled under the Labet name, here Aux Coucherias.
domaine-labet-beaune.tell: Aux Coucherias is a Beaune premier cru giving a balanced, red fruited wine. Ask the sommelier about this producer.

alex-foillard.name: Alex Foillard
alex-foillard.line: The son of Jean Foillard, making his own natural leaning cru Beaujolais, here Brouilly.
alex-foillard.tell: Alex Foillard is the son of Jean Foillard, one of the great Morgon names. His Brouilly is juicy, bright and fresh. Great with lighter dishes, and serve it slightly cool.

jean-foillard.name: Jean Foillard
jean-foillard.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Morgon, famous for the Côte du Py, making deep, fine, age worthy Gamay.
jean-foillard.tell: Foillard is one of the original Beaujolais growers who changed how the region is seen. Côte du Py is a famous hill in Morgon. The wines have depth and freshness; serve them slightly cool.

chateau-des-jacques.name: Château des Jacques
chateau-des-jacques.line: The Moulin-à-Vent estate owned by Louis Jadot, making structured, Burgundy minded cru Beaujolais.
chateau-des-jacques.tell: Château des Jacques is Jadot's Beaujolais estate. Moulin-à-Vent gives a firmer, deeper Gamay that can age. Clos du Grand Carquelin is one of their walled sites.

daniel-bouland.name: Daniel Bouland
daniel-bouland.line: A small Beaujolais grower making traditional, old vine cru wines, here Côte de Brouilly.
daniel-bouland.tell: Bouland is a small traditional grower. Côte de Brouilly comes from the slopes of Mont Brouilly. Fresh and fruity, a good value red.

domaine-coudert.name: Domaine Coudert
domaine-coudert.line: The Fleurie family domaine behind Clos de la Roilette, making firm, deep, age worthy Fleurie and Moulin-à-Vent.
domaine-coudert.tell: Coudert's Clos de la Roilette is a famous Fleurie site that gives a firmer, darker wine than most Fleurie. A great value red with poultry or pork.

jean-paul-thevenet.name: Domaine Jean-Paul Thévenet
jean-paul-thevenet.line: One of the founding natural wine growers of Morgon, making old vine, fresh, deep Gamay.
jean-paul-thevenet.tell: Thévenet was one of the original natural growers of Morgon. The old vine Morgon in magnum is a fun pick for a big table.

guy-breton.name: Guy Breton
guy-breton.line: One of the original natural wine growers of Morgon, making fresh, joyful Gamay.
guy-breton.tell: Guy Breton was one of the founding natural growers in Beaujolais. P'tit Max is his Morgon. Fresh, juicy and delicious slightly cool.

jean-claude-lapalu.name: Jean-Claude Lapalu
jean-claude-lapalu.line: A Brouilly grower making natural leaning, characterful cru Beaujolais.
jean-claude-lapalu.tell: Lapalu makes characterful Brouilly with plenty of energy. A fun, fresh red for a curious guest.

jules-desjourneys.name: Jules Desjourneys
jules-desjourneys.line: A Beaujolais grower making serious, structured cru wines, here Fleurie.
jules-desjourneys.tell: Desjourneys makes deep, structured Beaujolais that is priced more like Burgundy. Les Moriers is a Fleurie site. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

la-soeur-cadette.name: La Soeur Cadette
la-soeur-cadette.line: A small négociant run by Valentin Montaney, buying grapes from Burgundy and Beaujolais, here Juliénas.
la-soeur-cadette.tell: La Soeur Cadette is a small négociant. Their Juliénas is bright and juicy, textbook cru Beaujolais. Great value and slightly cool.

marcel-lapierre.name: Marcel Lapierre
marcel-lapierre.line: The Morgon domaine of the late Marcel Lapierre, pioneer of natural Beaujolais, now run by his children.
marcel-lapierre.tell: Lapierre is the name most associated with natural Beaujolais. The Morgon is fresh, silky and delicious. Serve it slightly cool.

paul-janin.name: Paul Janin
paul-janin.line: A Moulin-à-Vent family domaine making deep, structured Gamay from the Clos du Tremblay.
paul-janin.tell: Janin is a family grower in Moulin-à-Vent, the cru that gives the deepest Beaujolais. A great value red with meats.

marc-delienne.name: Marc Delienne
marc-delienne.line: A Fleurie grower making fresh, natural leaning Gamay.
marc-delienne.tell: Delienne makes lively, fresh Fleurie. Abbaye Road is his named cuvée. Fresh and fun, slightly cool.

chateau-de-breze.name: Château de Brezé
chateau-de-breze.line: A historic château estate in Saumur, making Cabernet Franc and Chenin Blanc from limestone slopes.
chateau-de-breze.tell: Brezé is a château in Saumur with deep limestone cellars, known for Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc. This Clos de l'Étoile is from 2014, so it has some age. Ask the sommelier how it is showing before recommending it.

catherine-et-pierre-breton.name: Catherine & Pierre Breton
catherine-et-pierre-breton.line: A Bourgueil couple farming biodynamically, among the best known natural leaning names in the Loire, making fresh, savoury Cabernet Franc.
catherine-et-pierre-breton.tell: The Bretons are leading growers in Bourgueil, and their Cabernet Franc is fresh, red fruited and a little herbal. Les Perrières is their serious, age worthy bottling; Franc de Pied comes from ungrafted vines. A great choice for a guest who likes lighter, savoury reds.

charles-joguet.name: Charles Joguet
charles-joguet.line: A leading Chinon domaine, making single vineyard Cabernet Franc in a structured, age worthy style.
charles-joguet.tell: Joguet is one of the most respected names in Chinon. The single vineyard wines, like Clos du Chêne Vert and Les Varennes du Grand Clos, have depth and structure. Cuvée Terroir is the fresher, younger one.

clos-rougeard.name: Clos Rougeard
clos-rougeard.line: The cult Saumur-Champigny estate built by the Foucault brothers, making some of the most sought after Cabernet Franc in the world; now owned by Martin Bouygues.
clos-rougeard.tell: Clos Rougeard is a legend among Loire lovers. Le Clos, Les Poyeaux and Le Bourg are long lived, fine Cabernet Franc that collectors chase. These are rare bottles; decant and treat them like great Burgundy.

roches-neuves.name: Domaine des Roches Neuves
roches-neuves.line: The Saumur domaine of Thierry Germain, farmed biodynamically, known for fresh, pure, lively Cabernet Franc.
roches-neuves.tell: Thierry Germain makes bright, pure Cabernet Franc in Saumur-Champigny. Terres Chaudes is a step up from the Domaine bottling. A great value red for poultry, pork or vegetables.

domaine-de-la-noblaie.name: Domaine de la Noblaie
domaine-de-la-noblaie.line: A Chinon family domaine making fresh and structured Cabernet Franc from tuffeau limestone.
domaine-de-la-noblaie.tell: Noblaie is a Chinon family estate. Le Temps des Cerises is a bright, cherry fruited Cabernet Franc meant to be enjoyed young. Lovely slightly cool.

yannick-amirault.name: Yannick Amirault
yannick-amirault.line: A leading Bourgueil grower farming organically, making deep, fine Cabernet Franc from named sites.
yannick-amirault.tell: Amirault is one of the top names in Bourgueil. His Cabernet Franc is deep and fine. A smart pick for a guest who likes Bordeaux but wants something lighter.

domaine-grosbois.name: Domaine Grosbois
domaine-grosbois.line: A Chinon family domaine farming organically and biodynamically, making fresh, characterful Cabernet Franc.
domaine-grosbois.tell: Grosbois is a Chinon family estate. La Cuisine de Ma Mère is the easy, fresh one; Gabare is deeper. Both are friendly with food and great value.

domaine-de-l-ecu.name: Domaine de l'Écu
domaine-de-l-ecu.line: A biodynamic estate in the Muscadet country, best known for white, also making red such as this Pinot Noir sold as Vin de France.
domaine-de-l-ecu.tell: Domaine de l'Écu is known for its Muscadet. Ange is a Pinot Noir from the estate, bottled as Vin de France. Light and fresh; ask the sommelier how it is tasting.

david-sautereau.name: Domaine David Sautereau
david-sautereau.line: A Sancerre family domaine making white and red; red Sancerre is light, fresh Pinot Noir.
david-sautereau.tell: Red Sancerre is Pinot Noir from the Loire: light, fresh and red fruited. A good choice for fish or chicken when a guest wants red.

alain-graillot.name: Alain Graillot
alain-graillot.line: The domaine that set the standard for Crozes-Hermitage, making fresh, whole cluster Syrah; now run by his son Maxime.
alain-graillot.tell: Graillot made Crozes-Hermitage famous for quality. The Syrah is fresh, peppery and dark fruited. A great value choice with lamb or steak.

andre-perret.name: André Perret
andre-perret.line: A northern Rhône grower known for Condrieu and fine, fresh Saint-Joseph Syrah.
andre-perret.tell: Perret is well known for white Condrieu, and his red Saint-Joseph is fresh and peppery. Les Grisières is an old vine bottling. Good with lamb.

auguste-clape.name: Auguste Clape
auguste-clape.line: The reference domaine of Cornas, making traditional, unfiltered Syrah of great depth that ages for decades.
auguste-clape.tell: Clape is the most respected name in Cornas. The wines are dark, savoury and powerful, made in a traditional way; Renaissance is the younger vines cuvée; Le Vin des Amis is their simple, friendly red, so decant the Cornas.

barruol-lynch.name: Barruol and Lynch
barruol-lynch.line: A partnership between Louis Barruol of Château de Saint Cosme and importer Kermit Lynch, making a Côte-Rôtie called Les Roses.
barruol-lynch.tell: Louis Barruol, who runs Saint Cosme in Gigondas, makes this Côte-Rôtie with the American importer Kermit Lynch. Expect perfumed, peppery Syrah. A good value Côte-Rôtie.

domaine-duclaux.name: Domaine Benjamin & David Duclaux
domaine-duclaux.line: A Côte-Rôtie family domaine run by brothers Benjamin and David Duclaux, making fragrant, traditional Syrah.
domaine-duclaux.tell: The Duclaux brothers make fragrant, fresh Côte-Rôtie. La Germine is their main cuvée. A good recommendation with lamb or duck.

bernard-faurie.name: Bernard Faurie
bernard-faurie.line: A small, traditional grower on the hill of Hermitage, making tiny amounts of classic Syrah.
bernard-faurie.tell: Faurie is a small traditional grower whose Hermitage is rare. The wine blends the Gréffieux and Bessards parcels on the hill. Powerful and savoury; decant it.

clusel-roch.name: Domaine Clusel-Roch
clusel-roch.line: A Côte-Rôtie family domaine farming organically, making fragrant, traditional Syrah from steep schist slopes.
clusel-roch.tell: Clusel-Roch is a Côte-Rôtie family estate. Classique is the entry wine, and Les Grandes Places is their famous old vine site. Peppery, floral Syrah.

georges-vernay.name: Domaine Georges Vernay
georges-vernay.line: The family domaine credited with saving Condrieu, now run by Christine Vernay, also making fine Côte-Rôtie and Saint-Joseph.
georges-vernay.tell: Vernay is famous for white Condrieu, and its reds are elegant. Maison Rouge and Blonde du Seigneur are Côte-Rôtie; Terre d'Encre is Saint-Joseph. Fragrant, fine Syrah.

jean-michel-stephan.name: Domaine Jean-Michel Stephan
jean-michel-stephan.line: A small Côte-Rôtie grower making natural leaning Syrah from named hillside sites.
jean-michel-stephan.tell: Stephan is a small Côte-Rôtie grower. Côteaux de Bassenon and Côteaux du Tupin are named slopes. Fragrant Syrah; ask the sommelier how these bottles are tasting.

guigal.name: E. Guigal
guigal.line: The most famous house of the northern Rhône, based in Ampuis, known for its single vineyard Côte-Rôtie La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque.
guigal.tell: Guigal is the big name of the Rhône, and the single vineyard Côte-Rôties, La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque, are among the most collected Rhône wines. Château d'Ampuis is a blend; Vignes de l'Hospice is their Saint-Joseph. Decant the big ones.

domaine-jamet.name: Domaine Jamet
domaine-jamet.line: A much admired Côte-Rôtie family domaine making traditional, whole cluster, savoury Syrah.
domaine-jamet.tell: Jamet is one of the great Côte-Rôtie names. Their Syrah is peppery, floral and savoury. The Côtes du Rhône is a lovely value way into their style.

lionel-faury.name: Lionel Faury
lionel-faury.line: A northern Rhône family domaine making fresh Saint-Joseph and Côte-Rôtie.
lionel-faury.tell: Faury is a northern Rhône family grower. Les 3 Brunes is a Côte-Rôtie. Fresh, peppery Syrah.

rene-rostaing.name: René Rostaing
rene-rostaing.line: A top Côte-Rôtie domaine, now run by Pierre Rostaing, making fine, elegant Syrah including Côte Blonde and La Landonne.
rene-rostaing.tell: Rostaing is a leading Côte-Rôtie name, and Côte Blonde is the softer, more perfumed side of the appellation; La Landonne is the darker, firmer side. Ampodium is their blend; decant.

delas-freres.name: Delas Frères
delas-freres.line: A Rhône négociant and grower based near Hermitage, making wines across the northern and southern Rhône.
delas-freres.tell: Delas is a well known Rhône house. Sainte-Épine is a Saint-Joseph, and Haute Pierre is a Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Reliable, good value.

les-alexandrins.name: Domaine Les Alexandrins
les-alexandrins.line: A northern Rhône producer making Saint-Joseph and other northern appellations.
les-alexandrins.tell: Saint-Joseph gives fresh, peppery Syrah at fair prices. A good value Syrah for steak.

pierre-gonon.name: Pierre Gonon
pierre-gonon.line: A Saint-Joseph family domaine, much admired for traditional, fragrant Syrah.
pierre-gonon.tell: Gonon is one of the most admired names in Saint-Joseph. Their Syrah is fragrant, peppery and fresh. Note the list spells it Gonan.

domaine-de-la-chapelle.name: Domaine de la Chapelle
domaine-de-la-chapelle.line: The estate created by the Frey family, owners of Paul Jaboulet Aîné, to make the famous Hermitage La Chapelle from the 2021 vintage on.
domaine-de-la-chapelle.tell: Hermitage La Chapelle was Jaboulet's famous wine; from 2021 it is made under the Domaine de la Chapelle name. Deep, powerful Syrah from the hill of Hermitage. Decant.

jean-louis-chave.name: Domaine Jean-Louis Chave
jean-louis-chave.line: The great family domaine of Hermitage, whose blended Hermitage is one of the most revered wines of the Rhône.
jean-louis-chave.tell: Chave is the most respected name on the hill of Hermitage. Their Hermitage blends several parcels into a deep, long lived Syrah. A trophy bottle; decant.

paul-jaboulet-aine.name: Paul Jaboulet Aîné
paul-jaboulet-aine.line: The historic northern Rhône house, owned by the Frey family since 2006, whose Hermitage La Chapelle is one of the great Rhône names.
paul-jaboulet-aine.tell: La Chapelle is Jaboulet's famous Hermitage. These bottles predate the move to the Domaine de la Chapelle label. Deep, savoury Syrah; ask the sommelier about the vintage.

dard-et-ribo.name: Dard & Ribo
dard-et-ribo.line: A cult natural leaning domaine in Crozes-Hermitage, making fresh, juicy Syrah with little intervention.
dard-et-ribo.tell: Dard & Ribo makes fresh, lively Syrah in Crozes-Hermitage. C'est le Printemps is their bright, spring-like red. Fun and food friendly.

etienne-becheras.name: Étienne Bécheras
etienne-becheras.line: A small Crozes-Hermitage grower making natural leaning Syrah.
etienne-becheras.tell: Bécheras is a small Crozes grower. Le Prieuré d'Arras is a fresh, peppery Syrah. A good value pick.

laurent-combier.name: Laurent Combier
laurent-combier.line: A leading Crozes-Hermitage family domaine farming organically, making ripe, fresh Syrah.
laurent-combier.tell: Combier is one of the best known names in Crozes-Hermitage. Expect ripe, dark fruited Syrah. A good value choice with steak.

domaine-du-coulet.name: Domaine du Coulet
domaine-du-coulet.line: A Cornas domaine run by Matthieu Barret, farming biodynamically, making fresh, vibrant Syrah.
domaine-du-coulet.tell: Coulet makes a fresher, brighter style of Cornas. Brise Cailloux is their main Cornas. Good with lamb.

ferraton.name: Ferraton Père & Fils
ferraton.line: A northern Rhône house, linked to Chapoutier, farming biodynamically and making wines across the northern appellations.
ferraton.tell: Ferraton is a northern Rhône house. Les Grands Mûriers is a Cornas. Dark, powerful Syrah.

guillaume-gilles.name: Guillaume Gilles
guillaume-gilles.line: A small Cornas grower making traditional, deep Syrah.
guillaume-gilles.tell: Gilles is a small Cornas grower who makes classic, dark, savoury Syrah. A good pick for lamb or game.

thierry-allemand.name: Thierry Allemand
thierry-allemand.line: A cult Cornas grower making tiny amounts of pure, deep Syrah from Chaillot and Reynard.
thierry-allemand.tell: Allemand is a cult name in Cornas. Les Chaillot is the fresher one; Reynard is deeper. Rare bottles; decant.

chapelle-st-theodoric.name: Chapelle St. Théodoric
chapelle-st-theodoric.line: A small Châteauneuf-du-Pape producer making Grenache led wines from sandy sites.
chapelle-st-theodoric.tell: A small Châteauneuf producer. Le Grand Pin is a Grenache led wine. Ask the sommelier for the story.

chateau-de-beaucastel.name: Château de Beaucastel
chateau-de-beaucastel.line: The Perrin family's famous Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate, known for using all permitted grapes and a high share of Mourvèdre; Coudoulet is its Côtes du Rhône.
chateau-de-beaucastel.tell: Beaucastel is one of Châteauneuf's great names, and Hommage à Jacques Perrin is their rare, Mourvèdre rich top wine. Coudoulet is the Côtes du Rhône from vines next door, and Oenothèque bottles are older releases from the estate's cellar.

famille-perrin.name: Famille Perrin
famille-perrin.line: The Perrin family's négociant range, from the owners of Château de Beaucastel.
famille-perrin.tell: The Perrin family, of Beaucastel, make this Côtes du Rhône-Villages. The half bottle is a handy, easy red.

chateau-la-nerthe.name: Château La Nerthe
chateau-la-nerthe.line: A historic Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate making classic Grenache led wines.
chateau-la-nerthe.tell: La Nerthe is one of Châteauneuf's historic estates. Expect a rich, warm red with dark fruit and spice. Good with lamb.

chateau-rayas.name: Château Rayas
chateau-rayas.line: The cult Châteauneuf-du-Pape estate of the Reynaud family, famous for pure, fragrant Grenache from sandy soils; also Pignan, Fonsalette and La Pialade.
chateau-rayas.tell: Rayas is the most cult name in Châteauneuf, and the Grenache is fine and fragrant, more Burgundy than Rhône. Pignan comes from the same family; Fonsalette and La Pialade are their Côtes du Rhône, all of them rare.

chateau-saint-cosme.name: Château de Saint Cosme
chateau-saint-cosme.line: The historic Gigondas estate of Louis Barruol, making fine, spicy Gigondas and also a Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
chateau-saint-cosme.tell: Saint Cosme is the leading name in Gigondas. Their Gigondas is spicy and deep. The magnum is great for a big table.

domaine-de-beaurenard.name: Domaine de Beaurenard
domaine-de-beaurenard.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine farming biodynamically, making balanced, fresh Grenache led wines.
domaine-de-beaurenard.tell: Beaurenard is a family estate in Châteauneuf. Their wine is balanced and spicy. A good value Châteauneuf.

domaine-charvin.name: Domaine Charvin
domaine-charvin.line: A traditional Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine making pure, unoaked Grenache led wine.
domaine-charvin.tell: Charvin is a traditional Châteauneuf family. The wine is pure, fresh and fragrant, made without new oak. A great choice for lamb.

clos-du-caillou.name: Domaine du Clos du Caillou
clos-du-caillou.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine at Courthézon making rich Grenache led wines; the Réserve is its top bottling.
clos-du-caillou.tell: Clos du Caillou makes rich, deep Châteauneuf. The Réserve is their top cuvée, and this bottle has some age. Ask the sommelier how it is drinking.

domaine-de-la-charbonniere.name: Domaine de la Charbonnière
domaine-de-la-charbonniere.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine also making Vacqueyras, in a ripe, generous style.
domaine-de-la-charbonniere.tell: Charbonnière is a family estate. Their Châteauneuf is ripe and warm, and the Vacqueyras Cuvée Spéciale is a good value alternative. Good with lamb.

domaine-de-marcoux.name: Domaine de Marcoux
domaine-de-marcoux.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine farming biodynamically, known for fragrant old vine Grenache.
domaine-de-marcoux.tell: Marcoux is a family estate known for its old vine Châteauneuf. The Vieilles Vignes is fragrant and deep. A special Rhône bottle.

clos-saint-jean.name: Clos Saint Jean
clos-saint-jean.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine known for rich, ripe, powerful top cuvées.
clos-saint-jean.tell: Clos Saint Jean makes rich, powerful Châteauneuf. La Combe des Fous and Sanctus Sanctorum are their top cuvées. Big wines for big meats.

domaine-de-ferrand.name: Domaine de Ferrand
domaine-de-ferrand.line: A small Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine making Grenache led wine.
domaine-de-ferrand.tell: A small Châteauneuf estate. Expect a warm, spicy Grenache led red. A good value Châteauneuf.

vieille-julienne.name: Domaine de la Vieille Julienne
vieille-julienne.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine farming biodynamically, making fine, fragrant Grenache.
vieille-julienne.tell: Vieille Julienne makes fine, fragrant Châteauneuf. Les Trois Sources and the Réservé are their bottlings. A strong pick for lamb.

domaine-du-pegau.name: Domaine du Pegau
domaine-du-pegau.line: The Féraud family's traditional Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine, known for powerful, savoury, old school Grenache; Château Pégau is a related family estate.
domaine-du-pegau.tell: Pégau is one of the most traditional names in Châteauneuf. Cuvée Réservée is the main wine; Cuvée Laurence spends longer in barrel. Big, savoury reds; large formats here are great for a big table.

vieux-telegraphe.name: Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe
vieux-telegraphe.line: The Brunier family's Châteauneuf-du-Pape domaine on the stony La Crau plateau, making powerful, long lived reds.
vieux-telegraphe.tell: Vieux Télégraphe is one of Châteauneuf's best known names. La Crau is their stony plateau vineyard. Deep, spicy and long lived.

raymond-usseglio.name: Domaine Raymond Usseglio & Fils
raymond-usseglio.line: A Châteauneuf-du-Pape family domaine making Grenache led wines; Cuvée Impériale is its old vine top wine.
raymond-usseglio.tell: Usseglio is a family estate in Châteauneuf. Cuvée Girard and Cuvée Impériale are old vine Grenache led wines. Rich, spicy and generous.

isabel-ferrando.name: Famille Isabel Ferrando
isabel-ferrando.line: The family label of Isabel Ferrando, known for Domaine Saint-Préfert in Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
isabel-ferrando.tell: Isabel Ferrando is a respected Châteauneuf grower. Expect a fragrant, fine Grenache led red. A good pick for lamb.

chateau-des-tours.name: Château des Tours
chateau-des-tours.line: The Vacqueyras estate of Emmanuel Reynaud of Château Rayas, making fragrant Grenache in a similar spirit.
chateau-des-tours.tell: Château des Tours is run by the same hand as Rayas. The Vacqueyras and Côtes du Rhône are fragrant, pure Grenache. A great value way into the Rayas style.

domaine-de-durban.name: Domaine de Durban
domaine-de-durban.line: A Beaumes-de-Venise family domaine, known for sweet Muscat, also making red.
domaine-de-durban.tell: Durban is known for its sweet Muscat. Their red Beaumes-de-Venise is warm and spicy. Good value.

raspail-ay.name: Domaine Raspail-Ay
raspail-ay.tell: Raspail-Ay is a traditional Gigondas family. Expect a warm, spicy red. The half bottle is handy for a couple.

domaine-saint-damien.name: Domaine Saint Damien
domaine-saint-damien.line: A Gigondas family domaine making old vine, Grenache led wines.
domaine-saint-damien.tell: Saint Damien makes old vine Gigondas, rich, spicy and good value. Ask the sommelier where the name of La Louisianne comes from; a Louisiana link would be a good story to tell, if it is true.

domaine-viret.name: Domaine Viret
domaine-viret.line: A southern Rhône family domaine practising its own form of biodynamic farming, here a Vin de France.
domaine-viret.tell: Viret is an unusual southern Rhône estate with its own farming philosophy. Renaissance is a deep, spicy red. Ask the sommelier about how it is made.

gourt-de-mautens.name: Gourt de Mautens
gourt-de-mautens.line: A small Rasteau domaine, run by Jérôme Bressy, making deep, fine Grenache led wine sold under a regional name.
gourt-de-mautens.tell: Gourt de Mautens is a much admired small estate near Rasteau. Expect a deep, fragrant Grenache led wine. The magnum is great for a big table.

rolly-gassmann.name: Rolly Gassmann
rolly-gassmann.line: An Alsace family domaine famous for whites, also making Pinot Noir.
rolly-gassmann.tell: Alsace Pinot Noir is light and fresh. Rolly Gassmann is a well known family. A good lighter red.

domaine-du-pelican.name: Domaine du Pélican
domaine-du-pelican.line: The Jura estate of the Marquis d'Angerville family from Volnay, making fresh, fine Jura reds.
domaine-du-pelican.tell: Pélican is owned by the d'Angerville family of Volnay. Their Jura Pinot Noir and blends are light and fresh. A great choice for a Burgundy lover.

domaine-labet.name: Domaine Labet
domaine-labet.line: A Jura family domaine known for natural leaning, fresh wines.
domaine-labet.tell: Labet is a Jura family estate. Les Varrons Massale is a Pinot Noir from the Côtes du Jura. Light and fresh.

rousset-martin.name: François Rousset-Martin
rousset-martin.line: A small Jura grower making natural leaning, characterful wines.
rousset-martin.tell: Rousset-Martin is a small Jura grower. Voyage au bout de Nuits is a Pinot Noir. Light, fresh and curious.

ganevat.name: Jean-François Ganevat
ganevat.line: A cult Jura grower making natural leaning wines, many sold as Vin de France.
ganevat.tell: Ganevat is a cult name in the Jura. De Toute Beauté is a Vin de France red. Light, fresh and fragrant.

chateau-pradeaux.name: Château Pradeaux
chateau-pradeaux.line: A traditional Bandol estate making powerful, long lived Mourvèdre.
chateau-pradeaux.tell: Pradeaux is a traditional Bandol estate. The Mourvèdre is powerful and savoury and needs age. This bottle has some.

bastide-blanche.name: Domaine de la Bastide Blanche
bastide-blanche.line: A Bandol family domaine making Mourvèdre led reds from named cuvées.
bastide-blanche.tell: Bastide Blanche is a Bandol family estate. Estagnol and Fontanéou are their cuvées. Dark, savoury Mourvèdre.

domaine-de-trevallon.name: Domaine de Trévallon
domaine-de-trevallon.line: The cult Provence estate founded by Éloi Dürrbach, blending Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah in the Alpilles.
domaine-de-trevallon.tell: Trévallon is a famous Provence estate blending Cabernet and Syrah. Deep, savoury and long lived. A good value choice for a Bordeaux drinker.

domaine-tempier.name: Domaine Tempier
domaine-tempier.line: The famous Bandol domaine of the Peyraud family, making Mourvèdre led reds from named sites.
domaine-tempier.tell: Tempier is the most famous name in Bandol. La Migoua and La Tourtine are single site wines; Lulu et Lucien is a special cuvée. Big, savoury reds for lamb.

tour-du-bon.name: Domaine de la Tour du Bon
tour-du-bon.line: A Bandol domaine making Mourvèdre led reds.
tour-du-bon.tell: Tour du Bon is a Bandol estate. Saint Ferréol is a Mourvèdre led red. Savoury and dark.

domaine-d-aupilhac.name: Domaine d'Aupilhac
domaine-d-aupilhac.line: A Montpeyroux domaine run by Sylvain Fadat, farming organically and making deep southern French reds.
domaine-d-aupilhac.tell: Aupilhac is a respected Languedoc estate. Expect a deep, spicy southern red. A great value choice.

grange-des-peres.name: Domaine de la Grange des Pères
grange-des-peres.line: The cult Languedoc estate of Laurent Vaillé, blending Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cabernet Sauvignon.
grange-des-peres.tell: Grange des Pères is the cult wine of the Languedoc. Deep, fine and long lived. Rare bottles; decant.

domaine-ledogar.name: Domaine Ledogar
domaine-ledogar.line: A Corbières family domaine making natural leaning southern reds.
domaine-ledogar.tell: Ledogar is a Corbières family estate. Le Mariole is Carignan. Fresh, juicy and fun.

benoit-lahaye.name: Benoît Lahaye
benoit-lahaye.line: A Bouzy grower in Champagne, also making a still red Coteaux Champenois.
benoit-lahaye.tell: Lahaye is a Champagne grower in Bouzy. Bouzy Rouge is a still red Pinot Noir from Champagne. Rare and fresh.

bollinger.name: Bollinger
bollinger.line: The great Aÿ Champagne house, also making a still red Coteaux Champenois from La Côte aux Enfants.
bollinger.tell: Bollinger is a great Champagne house. La Côte aux Enfants is a still red Pinot Noir from Aÿ. A rare treat.

egly-ouriet.name: Egly-Ouriet
egly-ouriet.line: A top Ambonnay grower, also making still red Coteaux Champenois.
egly-ouriet.tell: Egly-Ouriet is a top Champagne grower. Their still red Pinot Noir is rare and fine.

chateau-du-cedre.name: Château du Cèdre
chateau-du-cedre.line: A leading Cahors estate making deep Malbec.
chateau-du-cedre.tell: Du Cèdre is a leading Cahors estate. Cahors is Malbec from France: dark, firm and savoury. Good with steak.

crocus.name: Crocus
crocus.line: A Cahors project of Paul Hobbs with Bertrand-Gabriel Vigouroux, making Malbec.
crocus.tell: Crocus is a Cahors Malbec from the American winemaker Paul Hobbs and a local partner. L'Atelier is the entry wine. Dark and juicy.

comte-abbatucci.name: Domaine Comte Abbatucci
comte-abbatucci.line: A biodynamic Corsican estate known for reviving native grapes.
comte-abbatucci.tell: Abbatucci is a famous Corsican estate. Ministre Impérial is a blend of native grapes. Fragrant and fine.

louis-magnin.name: Domaine Louis Magnin
louis-magnin.line: A Savoie family domaine making mountain reds.
louis-magnin.tell: Magnin is a Savoie family estate. Expect a light, fresh mountain red. A curious pick.

chateau-calon-segur.name: Château Calon-Ségur
chateau-calon-segur.line: A Saint-Estèphe third growth famous for the heart on its label, making firm, long lived Cabernet led wines.
chateau-calon-segur.tell: Calon-Ségur is the château with the heart on the label, a lovely story for a celebration. Saint-Estèphe gives firm, structured Cabernet that ages for decades. A great anniversary bottle.

chateau-cos-labory.name: Château Cos Labory
chateau-cos-labory.line: A Saint-Estèphe fifth growth neighbouring Cos d'Estournel, making classic, firm claret at fair prices.
chateau-cos-labory.tell: Cos Labory sits next door to Cos d'Estournel and gives classic Saint-Estèphe at a gentler price. The magnum is a fine pick for a table of four or more.

chateau-cos-d-estournel.name: Château Cos d'Estournel
chateau-cos-d-estournel.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth, known for its pagoda towered chai, making rich, exotic, polished Cabernet and Merlot blends.
chateau-cos-d-estournel.tell: Cos d'Estournel is the leading name in Saint-Estèphe, famous for its oriental style towers. The wine is rich and polished, more opulent than most of its neighbours. Decant younger vintages; the magnums are perfect for big celebrations.

chateau-montrose.name: Château Montrose
chateau-montrose.line: A Saint-Estèphe second growth on gravel near the Gironde estuary, known for powerful, long lived Cabernet led wines.
chateau-montrose.tell: Montrose overlooks the Gironde and makes one of the most powerful wines of the Médoc. It needs time and rewards it. Decant, and pair with beef or lamb.

chateau-meyney.name: Château Meyney
chateau-meyney.line: A Saint-Estèphe estate near the Gironde; La Chapelle de Meyney is its second wine.
chateau-meyney.tell: La Chapelle de Meyney is the second wine of Château Meyney in Saint-Estèphe. It is a softer, earlier drinking claret at a friendly price.

chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.name: Château Grand-Puy-Lacoste
chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Borie family, admired for classic, cassis scented, honest Pauillac at a fair price.
chateau-grand-puy-lacoste.tell: Grand-Puy-Lacoste is classic Pauillac, Cabernet with cassis and cedar, owned by the same family as Ducru-Beaucaillou. Many think it drinks above its classification. A strong value for steak.

chateau-haut-bages-liberal.name: Château Haut-Bages Libéral
chateau-haut-bages-liberal.line: A Pauillac fifth growth with vines near Latour, making firm, fresh Cabernet led wine.
chateau-haut-bages-liberal.tell: Haut-Bages Libéral is a fifth growth with some vines near Château Latour. It gives classic, firm Pauillac at a sensible price. Good with red meat.

chateau-lafite-rothschild.name: Château Lafite Rothschild
chateau-lafite-rothschild.line: The first growth of Pauillac owned by the Rothschild family since 1868, famous for its elegance and perfume.
chateau-lafite-rothschild.tell: Lafite is perhaps the most famous name in Bordeaux. It is a first growth known for elegance and fragrance rather than raw power. These are trophy bottles: involve the sommelier, decant, and let the moment breathe.

domaines-barons-de-rothschild.name: Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite), Légende range
domaines-barons-de-rothschild.line: The Légende wines from the Lafite Rothschild family company, appellation blends made to show each Bordeaux appellation's character.
domaines-barons-de-rothschild.tell: Légende Pauillac comes from the family that owns Château Lafite. It is a friendly, Cabernet led Pauillac at an approachable price. A good way to give a guest the Lafite connection without the first growth price.

chateau-latour.name: Château Latour
