chateau-latour.line: The Pauillac first growth beside the Gironde, owned by the Pinault family, famous for powerful, long lived Cabernet.
chateau-latour.tell: Latour is the most powerful of the first growths, famed for consistency and longevity. The estate releases its wines only when it judges them ready. Decant, and serve with beef or lamb.

chateau-lynch-bages.name: Château Lynch-Bages
chateau-lynch-bages.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Cazes family, much loved for rich, generous, cassis rich wine that drinks above its rank.
chateau-lynch-bages.tell: Lynch-Bages is one of the most loved names in Bordeaux, often compared with second growths. Rich, generous Cabernet with cassis and cedar. The magnum is a great pick for a celebration.

chateau-duhart-milon.name: Château Duhart-Milon
chateau-duhart-milon.line: A Pauillac fourth growth owned by the Lafite Rothschild family; Moulin de Duhart is its second wine.
chateau-duhart-milon.tell: Duhart-Milon is Lafite's sister estate in Pauillac, and Moulin de Duhart is its second wine. It is an easy, fair priced way into the Lafite family.

chateau-mouton-rothschild.name: Château Mouton Rothschild
chateau-mouton-rothschild.line: The Pauillac first growth, promoted in 1973, famous for its rich, opulent wine and labels painted by a different artist each year.
chateau-mouton-rothschild.tell: Mouton is the first growth with an artist's label every year, a great story at the table. The wine is rich and opulent. Ask the sommelier who painted this vintage's label, and decant.

chateau-pichon-lalande.name: Château Pichon Longueville Comtesse de Lalande
chateau-pichon-lalande.line: A Pauillac second growth facing Latour, owned by the Roederer Champagne family, known for silky, perfumed, Merlot rich Pauillac.
chateau-pichon-lalande.tell: Pichon Lalande is one of the most elegant Pauillacs, with more Merlot than most, which gives a silky texture. The half bottle is a beautiful option for two.

chateau-pedesclaux.name: Château Pedesclaux
chateau-pedesclaux.line: A Pauillac fifth growth that has been extensively renewed in recent years, making modern, polished Cabernet.
chateau-pedesclaux.tell: Pedesclaux is a fifth growth in Pauillac that has invested heavily recently. Expect a modern, polished Cabernet at a fair price.

chateau-pontet-canet.name: Château Pontet-Canet
chateau-pontet-canet.line: A Pauillac fifth growth owned by the Tesseron family, farmed biodynamically, making deep, pure, highly regarded Cabernet.
chateau-pontet-canet.tell: Pontet-Canet is famous for biodynamic farming and wines many rate alongside second growths. Deep, pure Cabernet. Decant younger vintages.

chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.name: Château Ducru-Beaucaillou
chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.line: A Saint-Julien second growth on the Gironde owned by the Borie family, known for refined, long lived Cabernet.
chateau-ducru-beaucaillou.tell: Ducru-Beaucaillou is one of Saint-Julien's great estates. The wine is refined, balanced and long lived. A classic choice for beef or lamb.

chateau-gruaud-larose.name: Château Gruaud-Larose
chateau-gruaud-larose.line: A Saint-Julien second growth making rich, firm, generous Cabernet led wine.
chateau-gruaud-larose.tell: Gruaud-Larose is a generous, full style of Saint-Julien. A great value second growth with steak.

chateau-lalande.name: Château Lalande
chateau-lalande.line: A Saint-Julien estate owned by the Meffre family since 1964, once part of Château Lagrange.
chateau-lalande.tell: Lalande is a family run Saint-Julien that was once part of Château Lagrange. It is classic, approachable claret at a friendly price.

chateau-lalande-borie.name: Château Lalande-Borie
chateau-lalande-borie.line: A Saint-Julien estate of the Borie family, owners of Ducru-Beaucaillou.
chateau-lalande-borie.tell: Lalande-Borie comes from the family that owns Ducru-Beaucaillou. It is a softer, earlier drinking Saint-Julien at a friendly price.

chateau-leoville-las-cases.name: Château Léoville Las Cases
chateau-leoville-las-cases.line: A Saint-Julien second growth run by the Delon family, beside Latour, often ranked with the first growths for power and longevity.
chateau-leoville-las-cases.tell: Las Cases is one of the most prestigious second growths, its Grand Enclos running right up to Latour. The wine is serious and long lived. Decant, and give it time in the glass.

chateau-leoville-poyferre.name: Château Léoville Poyferré
chateau-leoville-poyferre.line: A Saint-Julien second growth owned by the Cuvelier family, known for rich, plush, modern Cabernet.
chateau-leoville-poyferre.tell: Poyferré is the plushest of the three Léovilles. Rich, ripe and generous. A crowd pleasing second growth.

chateau-talbot.name: Château Talbot
chateau-talbot.line: A Saint-Julien fourth growth making round, generous, approachable claret.
chateau-talbot.tell: Talbot is a well known Saint-Julien with a round, friendly style. A good value classified growth.

chateau-cantenac-brown.name: Château Cantenac Brown
chateau-cantenac-brown.line: A Margaux third growth with a striking Tudor style château, making firm, structured Margaux.
chateau-cantenac-brown.tell: Cantenac Brown is a third growth in Margaux with a famously English looking château. Structured, fragrant claret.

chateau-des-eyrins.name: Château des Eyrins
chateau-des-eyrins.line: A small Margaux estate owned by Xavier and Julie Gonet-Médeville, with a prized parcel beside Château Margaux; La Closerie des Eyrins is its second wine.
chateau-des-eyrins.tell: Eyrins is a tiny Margaux estate with vines next to Château Margaux and Palmer. La Closerie des Eyrins is the second wine. Fragrant, fine Margaux at a fair price.

chateau-giscours.name: Château Giscours
chateau-giscours.line: A large Margaux third growth making generous, fragrant claret.
chateau-giscours.tell: Giscours is a big Margaux third growth, generous and fragrant. A good value classified growth.

chateau-cordet.name: Château Cordet
chateau-cordet.line: A small Margaux estate making approachable claret.
chateau-cordet.tell: Cordet is a small Margaux producer. A fragrant, approachable Margaux at a friendly price.

chateau-margaux.name: Château Margaux
chateau-margaux.line: The first growth of the Margaux appellation, famous for perfume and silk; Pavillon Rouge is its second wine.
chateau-margaux.tell: Château Margaux is the first growth of its appellation, famed for fragrance and silky elegance. Pavillon Rouge is the second wine, a gentler price for the same estate. Decant.

chateau-marquis-d-alesme.name: Château Marquis d'Alesme
chateau-marquis-d-alesme.line: A Margaux third growth, renewed in recent years, making fragrant, polished wine.
chateau-marquis-d-alesme.tell: Marquis d'Alesme is a third growth in Margaux. Fragrant, polished claret at a fair price.

chateau-palmer.name: Château Palmer
chateau-palmer.line: A Margaux third growth, farmed biodynamically, often priced beside the first growths, known for Merlot rich, perfumed, silky wine.
chateau-palmer.tell: Palmer is a third growth that often sells for close to first growth prices. Rich in Merlot, perfumed and silky. Historical XIX Century Wine is a special blend recalling an older Bordeaux custom; ask the sommelier about it.

chateau-rauzan-segla.name: Château Rauzan-Ségla
chateau-rauzan-segla.line: A Margaux second growth owned by the owners of Chanel, making fragrant, refined Margaux; Ségla is its second wine.
chateau-rauzan-segla.tell: Rauzan-Ségla is a second growth in Margaux, owned by the family behind Chanel. Fragrant and refined. Ségla is the second wine, a friendly price.

chateau-haut-brion.name: Château Haut-Brion
chateau-haut-brion.line: The only first growth outside the Médoc, in Pessac-Léognan, owned by Domaine Clarence Dillon; Bahans Haut-Brion was its second wine's name.
chateau-haut-brion.tell: Haut-Brion is the only first growth from Graves, with a smoky, earthy, silky style. Bahans Haut-Brion is the older name of the second wine. Decant.

chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.name: Château La Mission Haut-Brion
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.line: The great Pessac-Léognan estate across the road from Haut-Brion, under the same ownership, making rich, deep wines.
chateau-la-mission-haut-brion.tell: La Mission is Haut-Brion's neighbour, under the same owners, and in many years just as admired. Rich, deep and smoky. A trophy bottle.

chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.name: Château La Tour Haut-Brion
chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.line: A former classified Graves estate under the same ownership as La Mission Haut-Brion, now absorbed into La Mission's vineyard.
chateau-la-tour-haut-brion.tell: La Tour Haut-Brion was a sister estate of La Mission and no longer exists as a separate wine. This 1982 is a rare, mature bottle; ask the sommelier how it is showing.

chateau-pape-clement.name: Château Pape Clément
chateau-pape-clement.line: A historic Pessac-Léognan estate named after Pope Clement V, owned by Bernard Magrez, making rich, modern Graves.
chateau-pape-clement.tell: Pape Clément is named after a medieval pope who once owned the vineyard. Rich, smoky Graves. Good with beef.

chateau-belle-brise.name: Château Belle-Brise
chateau-belle-brise.line: A tiny Pomerol estate of about two hectares, owned by Henri-Bruno de Coincy, making fine, elegant Merlot.
chateau-belle-brise.tell: Belle-Brise is a tiny Pomerol estate near Le Pin, made in very small amounts. Elegant, fine Merlot. A rare find for a Pomerol lover.

chateau-bellegrave.name: Château Bellegrave
chateau-bellegrave.line: A small Pomerol estate making supple Merlot led wine.
chateau-bellegrave.tell: Bellegrave is a Pomerol, so expect soft, plummy Merlot. A gentle price for the appellation.

chateau-clinet.name: Château Clinet
chateau-clinet.line: A Pomerol estate on the high plateau, making rich, modern Merlot led wine.
chateau-clinet.tell: Clinet is a leading Pomerol, rich and plush. A great choice with duck or beef.

chateau-gombaude-guillot.name: Château Gombaude-Guillot
chateau-gombaude-guillot.line: A small family estate in Pomerol making Merlot led wine.
chateau-gombaude-guillot.tell: Gombaude-Guillot is a small family Pomerol. Soft, plummy Merlot. The several vintages here make for a good comparison.

chateau-lafleur.name: Château Lafleur
chateau-lafleur.line: A tiny, revered Pomerol estate of the Guinaudeau family, rich in Cabernet Franc, among the most sought after wines of Bordeaux.
chateau-lafleur.tell: Lafleur is a tiny Pomerol estate that collectors prize as highly as Pétrus. It has more Cabernet Franc than most Pomerol. Rare bottles; decant.

chateau-la-fleur-petrus.name: Château La Fleur-Pétrus
chateau-la-fleur-petrus.line: A Pomerol estate of the Moueix family, near Pétrus, making silky, fine Merlot.
chateau-la-fleur-petrus.tell: La Fleur-Pétrus belongs to the Moueix family and sits near Pétrus. Silky, fine Pomerol. A lovely choice for duck or beef.

chateau-l-eglise-clinet.name: Château L'Église-Clinet
chateau-l-eglise-clinet.line: A small Pomerol estate on the plateau, long run by the late Denis Durantou, making deep, fine wines.
chateau-l-eglise-clinet.tell: L'Église-Clinet is a small, much admired Pomerol. Deep, fine and long lived. A special bottle.

chateau-l-evangile.name: Château L'Évangile
chateau-l-evangile.line: A Pomerol estate owned by the Lafite Rothschild family, between Pétrus and Cheval Blanc, making rich, deep Merlot.
chateau-l-evangile.tell: L'Évangile is owned by the Lafite Rothschild family and sits between Pétrus and Cheval Blanc. Rich, deep Pomerol. Decant.

chateau-trotanoy.name: Château Trotanoy
chateau-trotanoy.line: A Pomerol estate of the Moueix family, making powerful, deep Merlot.
chateau-trotanoy.tell: Trotanoy is a Moueix Pomerol, powerful and deep. A great choice for a Pomerol lover.

vieux-chateau-certan.name: Vieux Château Certan
vieux-chateau-certan.line: A Pomerol estate run by the Thienpont family, with more Cabernet Franc than most, making fine, fragrant wine.
vieux-chateau-certan.tell: Vieux Château Certan, run by the Thienpont family, is one of Pomerol's great names. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

clos-l-eglise.name: Clos l'Église
clos-l-eglise.line: A small Pomerol estate on the plateau making rich Merlot led wine.
clos-l-eglise.tell: Clos l'Église is a small Pomerol estate. Rich, plummy Merlot. A good choice for duck.

petrus.name: Pétrus
petrus.line: The most famous wine of Pomerol, almost entirely Merlot from blue clay, among the most prized wines in the world.
petrus.tell: Pétrus is the most famous Pomerol, almost all Merlot from a blue clay plateau. A trophy bottle; involve the sommelier.

chateau-armens.name: Château Armens
chateau-armens.line: A Saint-Émilion estate in Saint-Pey-d'Armens owned by the Malet Roquefort family of Château La Gaffelière.
chateau-armens.tell: Armens is owned by the family behind La Gaffelière. A friendly, good value Saint-Émilion.

chateau-l-arrosee.name: Château L'Arrosée
chateau-l-arrosee.line: A Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé on the slopes below the town, making fresh, fine wine.
chateau-l-arrosee.tell: L'Arrosée is a classified Saint-Émilion. Fresh, fine Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

chateau-beau-sejour-becot.name: Château Beau-Séjour Bécot
chateau-beau-sejour-becot.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on the limestone plateau, owned by the Bécot family.
chateau-beau-sejour-becot.tell: Beau-Séjour Bécot is a premier grand cru on Saint-Émilion's limestone plateau. Fine, fresh Merlot and Cabernet Franc.

chateau-canon.name: Château Canon
chateau-canon.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel, making fine, fresh wine.
chateau-canon.tell: Canon is a premier grand cru on the limestone plateau, owned by the family behind Chanel. Fine, fragrant and fresh.

chateau-cheval-blanc.name: Château Cheval Blanc
chateau-cheval-blanc.line: The great Saint-Émilion estate, rich in Cabernet Franc, which stood at the top of the classification until it withdrew in 2022; Le Petit Cheval is its second wine.
chateau-cheval-blanc.tell: Cheval Blanc is one of the world's great wines, unusual for its high share of Cabernet Franc. Le Petit Cheval is the second wine. Decant.

chateau-figeac.name: Château Figeac
chateau-figeac.line: A Saint-Émilion estate on gravel, unusually rich in Cabernet, promoted to premier grand cru classé A in 2022.
chateau-figeac.tell: Figeac is unusual in Saint-Émilion for its high share of Cabernet. It was promoted to the top rank in 2022. Fine and long lived.

chateau-pavie.name: Château Pavie
chateau-pavie.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé A owned by the Perse family, making rich, powerful wine.
chateau-pavie.tell: Pavie is one of Saint-Émilion's top estates. Rich and powerful. Decant.

chateau-troplong-mondot.name: Château Troplong-Mondot
chateau-troplong-mondot.line: A Saint-Émilion premier grand cru classé on a high point of the appellation.
chateau-troplong-mondot.tell: Troplong-Mondot sits on one of the highest points in Saint-Émilion. The half bottle is a lovely treat for two.

chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.name: Château Tertre de la Mouleyre
chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.line: A small Saint-Émilion family estate run by Éric Jeanneteau.
chateau-tertre-de-la-mouleyre.tell: Tertre de la Mouleyre is a small family estate in Saint-Émilion. Fine, fresh Merlot.

chateau-lassegue.name: Château Lassègue
chateau-lassegue.line: A Saint-Émilion Grand Cru Classé; Les Cadrans de Lassègue is its second wine.
chateau-lassegue.tell: Les Cadrans de Lassègue is the second wine of Château Lassègue. Soft, friendly Saint-Émilion at a gentle price.

chateau-vieux-taillefer.name: Château Vieux Taillefer
chateau-vieux-taillefer.line: A small Saint-Émilion estate farmed organically, whose Pavillon de Taillefer is a Merlot Grand Cru.
chateau-vieux-taillefer.tell: Pavillon de Taillefer is the main wine of Château Vieux Taillefer, a small organic estate in Saint-Émilion. All Merlot, soft and plummy.

tertre-roteboeuf.name: Tertre Rôtebœuf
tertre-roteboeuf.line: A small, cult Saint-Émilion estate of François Mitjavile, making rich, exotic, much admired wine.
tertre-roteboeuf.tell: Tertre Rôtebœuf is a cult Saint-Émilion from François Mitjavile. Rich, exotic and fine. A special bottle.

chateau-bernon-becot.name: Château Bernon Bécot
chateau-bernon-becot.line: A Puisseguin-Saint-Émilion estate bought in 2015 by the Bécot family of Beau-Séjour Bécot.
chateau-bernon-becot.tell: Bernon Bécot is owned by the family behind Beau-Séjour Bécot. Soft, friendly Merlot at a gentle price.

chateau-chasse-spleen.name: Château Chasse-Spleen
chateau-chasse-spleen.line: A well known Moulis estate making classic, firm claret.
chateau-chasse-spleen.tell: Chasse-Spleen is one of the best known names in Moulis. Classic, firm claret at a fair price.

chateau-clarke.name: Château Clarke
chateau-clarke.line: A Listrac estate owned by the Edmond de Rothschild family, making Merlot rich claret.
chateau-clarke.tell: Clarke is a Listrac estate owned by a branch of the Rothschild family. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-de-camensac.name: Château de Camensac
chateau-de-camensac.line: A Haut-Médoc fifth growth making classic claret.
chateau-de-camensac.tell: Camensac is a fifth growth in the Haut-Médoc. Classic claret at a fair price.

chateau-la-lagune.name: Château La Lagune
chateau-la-lagune.line: A Haut-Médoc third growth near Bordeaux city, making fragrant, fine claret.
chateau-la-lagune.tell: La Lagune is a third growth in the southern Médoc. Fragrant and fine. The magnum is good for a table.

chateau-la-tour-carnet.name: Château La Tour Carnet
chateau-la-tour-carnet.line: A Haut-Médoc fourth growth owned by Bernard Magrez, making rich, modern claret.
chateau-la-tour-carnet.tell: La Tour Carnet is a classified Haut-Médoc. Rich, modern claret at a fair price.

chateau-la-vieille-forge.name: Château La Vieille Forge
chateau-la-vieille-forge.line: A Lalande-de-Pomerol estate making Merlot led wine.
chateau-la-vieille-forge.tell: Lalande-de-Pomerol sits next to Pomerol and gives soft Merlot at a gentler price. A good value choice.

chateau-les-grands-chenes.name: Château Les Grands Chênes
chateau-les-grands-chenes.line: A Médoc cru bourgeois making classic, approachable claret.
chateau-les-grands-chenes.tell: Les Grands Chênes is a Médoc cru bourgeois. Classic, approachable claret at a friendly price.

chateau-sociando-mallet.name: Château Sociando-Mallet
chateau-sociando-mallet.line: An unclassified Haut-Médoc estate built up by Jean Gautreau, often compared with classified growths.
chateau-sociando-mallet.tell: Sociando-Mallet is often rated alongside the classified growths. Cuvée Jean Gautreau honours the man who built the estate. Firm, long lived claret.

clos-manou.name: Clos Manou
clos-manou.line: A small family estate in the northern Médoc making carefully made claret.
clos-manou.tell: Clos Manou is a small Médoc estate. Petit Manou is the second wine. Good value claret.

clos-sainte-anne.name: Clos Sainte-Anne
clos-sainte-anne.line: A small Côtes de Bordeaux property of the Courselle family, making Merlot led red.
clos-sainte-anne.tell: Clos Sainte-Anne is a small family property in the Côtes de Bordeaux. Soft, Merlot led red, one of the best values on the list.

domaine-de-l-aurage.name: Domaine de l'Aurage
domaine-de-l-aurage.line: A Castillon estate run by Louis Mitjavile, son of François of Tertre Rôtebœuf, making rich Merlot led wine.
domaine-de-l-aurage.tell: L'Aurage is run by Louis Mitjavile, whose family makes Tertre Rôtebœuf. Rich, ripe Castillon. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red.title: Red Burgundy
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red.line: Pinot Noir from the Côte d'Or and its neighbours, with Gamay from Beaujolais at the end. Ask whether the guest wants light and fragrant or deep and firm, and the budget, before you name a village.

France ~ Loire ~ Red.title: Loire reds
France ~ Loire ~ Red.line: Mostly Cabernet Franc from Saumur, Chinon and Bourgueil: fresh, red fruited and a little herbal, lighter than Bordeaux. Good value, good with poultry and pork, and lovely slightly cool. Clos Rougeard is the rare treasure.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red.title: Rhône reds
France ~ Rhone ~ Red.line: North: peppery Syrah from Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Cornas and Saint-Joseph. South: warm, spicy Grenache blends from Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Gigondas. Ask whether the guest likes savoury and firm or ripe and generous.

France ~ Other ~ Red.title: Other French reds
France ~ Other ~ Red.line: The rest of France: Provence Bandol and Trévallon, the Languedoc, light Jura and Savoie reds, Cahors Malbec, Corsica and rare still reds from Champagne. Ask what the guest usually drinks and steer by weight.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red.title: Red Bordeaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red.line: Left Bank Cabernet from Saint-Estèphe, Pauillac, Saint-Julien, Margaux and Graves; Right Bank Merlot from Pomerol and Saint-Émilion. Ask the budget and whether the guest wants firm and classic or soft and plush.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Saumur-Champigny.title: Saumur-Champigny
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Saumur-Champigny.line: Cabernet Franc from the limestone around Saumur, fresh and red fruited, from good value to the cult Clos Rougeard. Steer lighter eaters here.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Bourgueil.title: Bourgueil
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Bourgueil.line: Firmer, darker Cabernet Franc from the Touraine. Breton and Amirault are the names; a smart swap for a Bordeaux drinker who wants something lighter.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Chinon.title: Chinon
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Chinon.line: Cabernet Franc from the Vienne valley: red cherry, pencil shavings and a fresh finish. Great value; Joguet is the classic name.

France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Muscadet & Sancer.title: Muscadet and Sancerre reds
France ~ Loire ~ Red ~ Muscadet & Sancer.line: Light Pinot Noir from the Loire's white wine country. Suggest for fish or chicken when a guest wants red.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bourgogne.title: Bourgogne and regional reds
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bourgogne.line: Regional Pinot Noir, Passe-Tout-Grains and Côte de Nuits-Villages from top growers: the cheapest route to a famous name. Good for guests who want Burgundy under a modest budget.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Marsannay.title: Marsannay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Marsannay.line: The northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits: light, crisp, red fruited Pinot Noir at fair prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin Premier.title: Fixin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin Premier.line: Sturdy, earthy reds from Gevrey's northern neighbour, including Gelin's Clos Napoléon. Good value for a guest who likes firm red.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin.title: Fixin
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Fixin.line: Village Fixin: sturdy, rustic Pinot Noir next to Gevrey at friendlier prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Ruchottes-Cham.title: Ruchottes-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Ruchottes-Cham.line: A small Gevrey grand cru on thin, rocky soil, giving fine, mineral wine. Rare; a collector's pick.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazis-Chambert.title: Mazis-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazis-Chambert.line: A Gevrey grand cru next to Clos de Bèze, dark and powerful. For guests who want depth.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Griotte-Chambe.title: Griotte-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Griotte-Chambe.line: The smallest Gevrey grand cru, often described as cherry scented and silky. Very rare.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin - C.title: Chambertin-Clos de Bèze grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin - C.line: One of Burgundy's two most famous Gevrey grand crus, majestic and long lived. Celebration price; decant.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Charmes-Chambe.title: Charmes-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Charmes-Chambe.line: The largest and most approachable Gevrey grand cru: generous, rounded fruit. The gentlest grand cru step for a Gevrey lover.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin Gra.title: Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambertin Gra.line: The king of Gevrey: powerful, deep and long lived. A celebration bottle; involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Latricières-Ch.title: Latricières-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Latricières-Ch.line: A Gevrey grand cru next to Chambertin, firm and spicy. Good for game and beef.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazoyères-Cham.title: Mazoyères-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mazoyères-Cham.line: A Gevrey grand cru that may also be sold as Charmes; rich and ripe. A relative value among grand crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chapelle-Chamb.title: Chapelle-Chambertin grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chapelle-Chamb.line: A Gevrey grand cru below Clos de Bèze, finer and more fragrant than most. Rare.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.title: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.line: Dark, firm Pinot Noir with structure; Clos Saint-Jacques, Cazetiers and Lavaux Saint-Jacques are the famous names. Ask the budget; this page runs from moderate to grand cru prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.title: Gevrey-Chambertin
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Gevrey-Chamber.line: Village Gevrey: the deepest, most structured Pinot Noir of the Côte de Nuits. A steady choice for steak.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos de la Roc.title: Clos de la Roche grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos de la Roc.line: Morey-Saint-Denis's greatest grand cru, deep and mineral. Dujac and Ponsot are the names.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Saint-Den.title: Clos Saint-Denis grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Saint-Den.line: A Morey grand cru, finer and more fragrant than Clos de la Roche. For guests who love perfume.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos des Lambr.title: Clos des Lambrays grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos des Lambr.line: A Morey grand cru almost wholly owned by one estate, fragrant and fine.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.title: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.line: Between Gevrey and Chambolle in style: fragrant fruit with structure. Good value premier crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.title: Morey-Saint-Denis
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Morey-Saint-De.line: Village Morey: fragrant, balanced Pinot Noir, often a better buy than its famous neighbours.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bonnes Mares G.title: Bonnes-Mares grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Bonnes Mares G.line: A grand cru shared by Chambolle and Morey, firmer and darker than Musigny. Celebration price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Musigny Grand.title: Musigny grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Musigny Grand.line: Chambolle's greatest grand cru, silk and perfume. Among the most prized wines on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.title: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.line: The most fragrant, silky Pinot Noir of the Côte de Nuits; Les Amoureuses is the famous name. For guests who love elegance.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.title: Chambolle-Musigny
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chambolle-Musi.line: Village Chambolle: perfumed, silky and light on its feet. Lovely with duck or chicken.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vougeot Premie.title: Vougeot premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vougeot Premie.line: Premier cru from the village of Vougeot outside the great Clos, fragrant and fine.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Vougeot G.title: Clos de Vougeot grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Clos Vougeot G.line: A large walled grand cru shared by many owners, so the producer matters most. Rich, firm wine; ask the budget and steer by name.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Echézeaux Gran.title: Échezeaux grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Echézeaux Gran.line: A Vosne grand cru, spicy and fragrant, often the gentlest priced grand cru from a great producer.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Grands-Echézea.title: Grands-Échezeaux grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Grands-Echézea.line: A smaller, deeper grand cru next to Clos de Vougeot. Celebration price.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Richebourg Gra.title: Richebourg grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Richebourg Gra.line: A Vosne grand cru of great richness and spice. Very high prices; involve the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Saint-.title: Romanée-Saint-Vivant grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Saint-.line: A Vosne grand cru of great finesse and perfume, below Romanée-Conti. Celebration only.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Conti.title: Romanée-Conti grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Romanée-Conti.line: The most famous vineyard in Burgundy, wholly owned by the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti. Only with the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ La Tâche Grand.title: La Tâche grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ La Tâche Grand.line: A Vosne grand cru wholly owned by the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, spicy and profound. Only with the sommelier.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.title: Vosne-Romanée premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.line: Velvety, spicy, refined Pinot Noir from Burgundy's most famous village. Beaux Monts, Brûlées and Suchots are names to know.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.title: Vosne-Romanée
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Vosne-Romanée.line: Village Vosne: silky, spicy Pinot Noir from the home of the grandest grand crus.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.line: Dark, firm, earthy Pinot Noir with structure; Les Saints-Georges and Vaucrains are famous. Good with beef and game.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Nuits-Saint-Ge.line: Village Nuits: sturdy, dark fruited Pinot Noir. A steady choice for red meat.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.title: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.line: Fresh, fine reds from the village behind Corton. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.title: Pernand-Vergelesses
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pernand-Vergel.line: Light, fresh reds from the village behind the hill of Corton. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Corton Grand C.title: Corton grand cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Corton Grand C.line: The only red grand cru of the Côte de Beaune, firm and earthy. Bressandes and Clos du Roi are the names; often the best value grand cru.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.title: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.line: Fresh, red fruited premier crus at gentle prices. Lavières is a name to know.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.title: Savigny-lès-Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Savigny-lès-Be.line: Village Savigny: light, fresh Pinot Noir and a reliable value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune Premier.title: Beaune premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune Premier.line: Round, red fruited Pinot Noir from the wine capital; the big houses own much of it. Good with poultry and pork.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune.title: Beaune
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaune.line: Village Beaune: soft, red fruited and approachable.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard Premie.title: Pommard premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard Premie.line: The firmest, darkest reds of the Côte de Beaune; Rugiens and Épenots are the famous names. Good with beef.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard.title: Pommard
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Pommard.line: Village Pommard: sturdy, dark fruited Pinot Noir. For guests who want body.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay Premier.title: Volnay premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay Premier.line: The most fragrant, silky reds of the Côte de Beaune; Clos des Chênes, Caillerets and Santenots are names to know. Lovely with poultry.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay.title: Volnay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Volnay.line: Village Volnay: fragrant, silky and charming.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Monthélie.title: Monthélie
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Monthélie.line: Volnay's neighbour, with similar charm at lower prices; rare Coche-Dury and Roulot bottlings sit here too.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Saint Aubin Pr.title: Saint-Aubin premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Saint Aubin Pr.line: Light, fresh reds from a side valley behind Puligny. Good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.title: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.line: Red Chassagne, firm and fresh, from a village better known for white. An insider's value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.title: Chassagne-Montrachet
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Chassagne-Mont.line: Village red Chassagne: bright, firm Pinot Noir from great white wine families.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Santenay.title: Santenay
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Santenay.line: Sturdy, fruity reds from the southern Côte de Beaune at fair prices.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges Premi.title: Maranges premier cru
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges Premi.line: The southernmost Côte de Beaune premier crus: sturdy, fruity and among the best values on the list.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges.title: Maranges
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Maranges.line: Village Maranges: firm, fruity and good value.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Other Côte d'O.title: Other Côte d'Or villages
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Other Côte d'O.line: Smaller villages and Côte Chalonnaise reds: Ladoix, Aloxe-Corton, Blagny, Chorey, Auxey-Duresses and Rully. A place for value and a few rarities.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mercurey.title: Mercurey
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Mercurey.line: Côte Chalonnaise Pinot Noir: sturdy, red fruited and modestly priced.

France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaujolais.title: Beaujolais
France ~ Burgundy ~ Red ~ Beaujolais.line: Gamay from the granite crus: Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent, Brouilly and more. Juicy, fresh and great value; serve slightly cool.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Côte-Rôtie.title: Côte-Rôtie
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Côte-Rôtie.line: Fragrant, peppery Syrah from steep slopes, often with a little Viognier. Guigal's single vineyards are the trophies. Ask the budget; decant older bottles.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ St.-Joseph.title: Saint-Joseph
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ St.-Joseph.line: Fresh, peppery Syrah from the west bank of the northern Rhône. Good value with lamb.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Hermitage.title: Hermitage
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Hermitage.line: Powerful, long lived Syrah from a single hill; Chave and La Chapelle are the great names. Celebration price.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Crozes-Hermitage.title: Crozes-Hermitage
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Crozes-Hermitage.line: Fresh, dark fruited Syrah around the hill of Hermitage. Good value.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Cornas.title: Cornas
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Cornas.line: The darkest, most powerful Syrah of the northern Rhône. Clape and Allemand are the names; decant.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Châteauneuf-du-Pa.title: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Châteauneuf-du-Pa.line: Warm, spicy Grenache led blends from the southern Rhône. Rayas is the rarity; Beaucastel and Pégau the classics. Ask whether the guest wants fresh or rich.

France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Other Côte Du Rhô.title: Other southern Rhône
France ~ Rhone ~ Red ~ Other Côte Du Rhô.line: Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Côtes du Rhône and Vin de France: warm, spicy reds, many from great Châteauneuf names. Great value.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Alsace & Lorraine.title: Alsace
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Alsace & Lorraine.line: Light, fresh Pinot Noir from a white wine region.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Jura.title: Jura
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Jura.line: Light, fresh Pinot Noir and blends from the Jura hills. For Burgundy lovers who like something different.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Provence.title: Provence
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Provence.line: Bandol Mourvèdre, firm and savoury, and Trévallon's Cabernet and Syrah. Good with lamb.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Languedoc-Roussil.title: Languedoc
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Languedoc-Roussil.line: Deep, spicy southern reds, including the cult Grange des Pères. Good value.

France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Other French ~ Re.title: Other French reds
France ~ Other ~ Red ~ Other French ~ Re.line: Cahors Malbec, Corsican, Savoie, Jura Vin de France and rare still reds from Champagne. Ask about the guest's taste and steer by weight.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Estèphe.title: Saint-Estèphe
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Estèphe.line: The firmest Left Bank Cabernet. Cos d'Estournel, Montrose and Calon-Ségur are the names. Good with beef.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pauillac.title: Pauillac
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pauillac.line: Home of three first growths, Lafite, Latour and Mouton: cassis, cedar and power. Ask the budget; from Légende to first growths.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Julien.title: Saint-Julien
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Julien.line: Balanced, refined Cabernet; Léoville Las Cases and Ducru-Beaucaillou are the names.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Margaux.title: Margaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Margaux.line: The most fragrant, silky Left Bank wines; Château Margaux and Palmer lead. For guests who love perfume.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Graves.title: Graves and Pessac-Léognan
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Graves.line: Smoky, earthy, silky claret; Haut-Brion and La Mission are the names.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pomerol.title: Pomerol
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Pomerol.line: Soft, plummy Merlot from a small plateau; Pétrus, Lafleur and VCC are the trophies. Ask the budget.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Émilion.title: Saint-Émilion
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Saint-Émilion.line: Merlot and Cabernet Franc on limestone and clay; Cheval Blanc, Figeac and Pavie lead. From friendly to celebration.

France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Other Bordeaux.title: Other Bordeaux
France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red ~ Other Bordeaux.line: Haut-Médoc, Moulis, Listrac, Castillon and the satellites: classic claret at friendly prices. A great place for value.
